        body = ""
        try:
            body = response.text or ""
        except Exception:  # pragma: no cover - defensive: unreadable body
            body = ""
        if body:
            parts.append(f"body={body[:AI_ERROR_BODY_MAX_CHARS]}")

    # Attributes exposed directly by the provider client errors.
    for attr in ("code", "param", "status_code", "request_id", "body"):
        value = getattr(ex, attr, None)
        if value is not None:
            parts.append(f"{attr}={value}")

    # The real root cause (DNS, connection refused, timeout, TLS, proxy, ...)
    # is usually chained on the provider error.
    cause = ex.__cause__ or ex.__context__
    if cause is not None:
        parts.append(f"cause={type(cause).__name__}: {cause}")

    return " | ".join(str(part) for part in parts)


class SmolAgent:
    """
    Async-only streaming chat agent with multi-step tool support.

    All logging, event fan-out, cancellation checkpoints and per-run
    analytics are delegated to :class:`AgentRunContext` (the unified
    agent runtime). Callers may pass their own context through
    ``config["run_context"]`` (e.g. to share a Socket.IO listener or a
    cancellation token) or plain listeners via ``config["event_listeners"]``.

    Conversation flow
    ```mermaid
        flowchart TD
            A[chat] --> B[Resolve AgentRunContext]
            B --> C[run_context.run - RUN_START]
            C --> D[Build OpenAI messages]
            D --> E[Initialize ToolCache]
            E --> F[Stream completion via guard_stream]
            F -->|chunk| F1[Accumulate chunk]
            F1 -->|flush| F2[Callback with FULL accumulated content]
            F --> G{finish_reason?}
            G -->|tool_calls| H[Check ToolCache]
            H -->|HIT| H1[Skip _execute_tool - use cached]
            H -->|HIT| H2[Emit TOOL_END with cached=true]
            H -->|HIT - ToolResponse| H3[No output re-emitted - first run delivered it]
            H -->|MISS| I[LoopGuard.check - depth & breadth & stuck]
            I -->|ok| J[Execute tool - TOOL_START/END/ERROR/LOGS + output]
            H1 --> K{Dual-response tool?}
            J --> K
            K -->|yes| K1[user_response - collapsible TOOL_END output property]
            K -->|yes| K2[Send llm_response as tool result to model only]
            K -->|no| K3[Send normalised result as tool result to model only]
            K1 --> L[Append to openai_messages]
            K2 --> L
            K3 --> L
            L --> F
            I -->|limit exceeded| M[Summarise tool usage and finish gracefully]
            G -->|stop / length| N[Append final LLM text to final_answer_content]
            N --> O[Append final AIMessage + return typed AgentRunResult]
            M --> O
            O --> P[Record usage + cache stats - RUN_END]
            F -->|cancelled| Q[RUN_CANCELLED - raise CancelledError]
            F -->|provider error| R[Verbose AI error log + client notice - raise]
    ```
    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        settings: CODXJuniorSettings,
        llm_model: Optional[str] = None,
        user: Optional[CodxUser] = None,
        system: Optional[str] = None,
        session: Optional[Any] = None,
    ) -> None:
        """
        Args:
            settings:  Project settings providing LLM configuration.
            llm_model: Optional model override.
            user:      Optional user (used for API key and analytics).
            system:    Optional extra system prompt content (appended after
                      chat_global_instructions).
            session:   Optional session context (injected for tools that need
                      access to current chat or session state).
        """
        self.tools: List[Dict[str, Any]] = TOOLS

        self.settings = settings
        self.llm_settings = settings.get_llm_settings(llm_model=llm_model)
        self.model: str = self.llm_settings.model
        self.user = user
        self.api_key: str = (
            user.api_key if user and user.api_key else self.llm_settings.api_key
        )
        self.base_url: str = self.llm_settings.api_url
        # Store extra system instructions; global instructions will be loaded
        # dynamically on each chat to ensure freshness
        self.extra_system: str = (system or "").strip()
        # Store session context for tools that need access to it
        self.session: Optional[Any] = session

        self.client = OpenAI(api_key=self.api_key, base_url=self.base_url)
        logger.info(
            "SmolAgent created. USER: %s, MODEL: %s, URL: %s, "
            "MAX_TOOL_CALLS: %s, MAX_ITERATIONS: %s",
            user.username if user else "NONE",
            self.model,
            self.base_url,
            self.llm_settings.max_tool_calls,
            self.llm_settings.max_iterations,
        )

    def _build_system_message(self) -> str:
        """
        Build the complete system message by combining:
        1. LLM settings system prompt (if any)
        2. chat_global_instructions (loaded fresh from GlobalSettings)
        3. Extra system instructions passed to __init__

        Returns:
            The complete system message string.
        """
        parts: List[str] = []

        # 1. LLM settings system prompt
        if self.llm_settings.system:
            parts.append(self.llm_settings.system.strip())

        # 2. chat_global_instructions (loaded fresh, not cached)
        global_instructions = _load_chat_global_instructions()
        if global_instructions:
            parts.append(global_instructions)

        # 3. Extra system instructions
        if self.extra_system:
            parts.append(self.extra_system)

        return "\n".join(parts).strip()

    # ── Public API ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

    async def chat(
        self,
        messages: List[Union[AIMessage, HumanMessage]],
        config: Optional[Dict[str, Any]] = None,
    ) -> AgentRunResult:
        """
        Run a streaming chat completion with iterative multi-step tool support.

        The whole run is wrapped in :meth:`AgentRunContext.run`, which emits
        ``RUN_START`` / ``RUN_END`` / ``RUN_ERROR`` / ``RUN_CANCELLED`` events
        with an analytics summary attached.

        Tool results are cached within this conversation to avoid re-execution
        if the model requests the same tool with identical arguments.

        Loop limits are handled gracefully: instead of raising, the run is
        stopped and a summary of the tools used is appended to the assistant
        answer (see :meth:`_summarize_tool_usage`). This keeps the work in the
        persisted message so the next iteration can continue without repeating
        the same tools.

        Cost limits are handled gracefully too: every round's cost (plus any
        cost reported by tools via :attr:`ToolResponse.cost`) is accumulated and
        returned in the typed :class:`AgentRunResult`. Once the chat reaches
        ``Chat.estimation_cost``, the run stops before executing further tools so
        the chat never exceeds its budget.

        Provider errors (connection refused, DNS, timeout, TLS, bad request,
        ...) are logged verbosely with a traceback and mirrored to the client
        before being re-raised (see :meth:`_log_ai_error`).

        Message Structure
        The response always appends a single final answer AIMessage containing
        the model's own text. Tool output is delivered separately as a
        collapsible message property (``ToolEvent.output``) instead of being
        merged into the content, so the client can decide how to render it.

        Args:
            messages: Conversation history as LangChain message objects.
            config:   Optional dict with keys: ``tools``, ``chat_id``,
                      ``cancellation_token``, ``headers``, ``callbacks``,
                      ``run_context`` (an :class:`AgentRunContext`),
                      ``event_listeners`` (list of event callables),
                      ``current_chat`` (the Chat object for context), and
                      ``vision_content`` (optional vision API content blocks).

        Returns:
            The typed :class:`AgentRunResult` for this run. Its ``messages``
            attribute contains the updated conversation (with the final
            assistant reply appended); ``cost`` carries the cost breakdown.

        Raises:
            CancelledError: If the request is cancelled by the caller.
        """
        config = config or {}
        self._preflight_limit_check()

        run_context = self._resolve_run_context(config)
        result: Optional[AgentRunResult] = None

        # run_context.run() emits RUN_* lifecycle events. It swallows
        # AgentCancelled (emitting RUN_CANCELLED), so we translate the
        # cancelled state back to the legacy CancelledError afterwards.
        with run_context.run():
            result = await self._run_chat_loop(messages, config, run_context)

        if run_context.token.cancelled or result is None:
            raise CancelledError(CANCELLED_MESSAGE)
        return result

    # ── Chat loop ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

    async def _run_chat_loop(
        self,
        messages: List[Union[AIMessage, HumanMessage]],
        config: Dict[str, Any],
        run_context: AgentRunContext,
    ) -> AgentRunResult:
        """
        Execute the iterative streaming/tool loop for one conversation.

        Response accumulation strategy:
        - ``thinking_content``: Accumulates the model's OWN text (reasoning)
          produced during tool-calling rounds. Streamed live to the client via
          send_callback and included in the final AIMessage. Tool output is NOT
          added here: dual-response tool ``user_response`` values are emitted on
          the ``TOOL_END`` event and attached to the response message as a
          collapsible property (``ToolEvent.output``).
        - ``final_answer_content``: Accumulates LLM text during the final
          round (after the model stops making tool calls).

        Message generation:
        - Always emits exactly one AIMessage containing thinking_content and
          final_answer_content. Since tool output is no longer merged into the
          content, the message may legitimately be empty (a run that only
          executed tools); the assistant message is still appended so callers
          can rely on ``messages[-1]``. All run information (cost, usage, tool
          summaries) is returned in the typed :class:`AgentRunResult`.

        Tool caching:
        - Identical tool calls (same name + args) are cached per conversation.
        - Cached results bypass LoopGuard checks (don't count towards limits).
        - Cached tool results are only reused for the model message; they do NOT
          re-emit tool output (the first execution already delivered it).

        Loop limits:
        - When LoopGuard raises, the loop is broken gracefully (no exception
          propagates) and a summary of the tools used is appended to
          ``thinking_content`` so it is streamed to the user and persisted in
          the final answer.

        Cost limits:
        - Every round is priced in cxjcoins from provider usage + model prices
          and accumulated into the chat total. When the chat reaches its
          ``estimation_cost``, the loop is broken gracefully (before running
          more tools) and a notice is appended to the answer.

        Args:
            messages:    Conversation history as LangChain message objects.
            config:      Chat configuration dict (see :meth:`chat`).
            run_context: Unified runtime context for this run.

        Returns:
            The typed :class:`AgentRunResult` for this run.

        Raises:
            AgentCancelled: If cancellation is requested mid-run.
        """
        chat_id: Optional[str] = config.get("chat_id")
        cancellation_token: Optional[CancellationToken] = config.get(
            "cancellation_token"
        )
        headers: Dict[str, str] = config.get("headers", {})
        # Profiles taking part in this turn, declared by the chat engine in an
        # internal header. It is consumed here (never forwarded to the provider)
        # because the agent — not the profile definition — decides which profile
        # tools are injected (see :meth:`_profile_tools_for_run`).
        profile_names: List[str] = self._pop_profile_names(headers)
        session_id: Optional[str] = headers.get("session_id")
        tags: str = self._build_tags(headers)
        headers["x-litellm-tags"] = tags

        # Inject session context into settings for tools that need it
        current_chat = config.get("current_chat")
        if self.session and current_chat:
            self.settings._active_session = self.session
            self.session._current_chat = current_chat

        send_callback = self._make_callback_sender(config.get("callbacks"))
        kwargs = self._build_request_kwargs(
            config.get("tools", []), profile_names=profile_names
        )
        # Build system message dynamically on each chat (fresh global instructions)
        system_message = self._build_system_message()
        openai_messages = to_openai_messages(messages, system=system_message)

        # Initialize LoopGuard with resolved limits from AISettings.
        # Priority: Model > Provider > Fallback.
        # These limits are enforced on every tool round to prevent runaway
        # execution or breadth violations.
        loop_guard = LoopGuard(
            max_iterations=self.llm_settings.max_iterations,
            max_tool_calls=self.llm_settings.max_tool_calls,
        )

        # Initialize tool cache for this conversation.
        # Cached results bypass LoopGuard checks and don't count towards limits.
        tool_cache = ToolCache()

        # Chat cost budget: seed the accumulated chat cost from Chat.cost, the
        # deletion-safe accumulator maintained by ChatManager. Falling back to
        # summing the message costs keeps this working for chats persisted
        # before the accumulator existed.
        chat_cost: float = self._accumulated_chat_cost(current_chat)
        # Cost of THIS run (this SmolAgent iteration).
        iteration_cost: float = 0.0

        # Typed run accumulators (replace the previous additional_kwargs contract).
        # They feed the returned AgentRunResult.cost breakdown.
        total_input_tokens: int = 0
        total_output_tokens: int = 0
        total_input_cost: float = 0.0
        total_output_cost: float = 0.0
        total_tool_cost: float = 0.0
        tool_cost_by_name: Dict[str, float] = {}

        request_start = time.monotonic()

        # Track whether any tools were used in this conversation.
        tools_were_used: bool = False

        # thinking_content: accumulates the model's OWN text (reasoning) during
        # tool-calling rounds. Streamed live to client AND included in the final
        # AIMessage. Tool output is NOT added here — it is delivered via the
        # TOOL_END event as a collapsible message property (ToolEvent.output).
        # final_answer_content: the final LLM response after all tool calls.
        thinking_content: str = ""
        final_answer_content: str = ""

        # Set when LoopGuard stops the run. The loop is then broken gracefully
        # and a tool-usage summary is produced so the work is not lost.
        loop_limit_error: Optional[str] = None

        # Set when the chat reaches its estimated cost. The loop is then broken
        # gracefully (before executing more tools) and a notice is appended.
        cost_limit_error: Optional[str] = None

        # Initialised before the loop so they are always defined for the
        # post-loop analytics call, even when the very first budget check stops
        # the run before any completion is performed.
        request_id: Optional[str] = None
        usage_info: Any = None

        # Extract vision content from config (optional)
        vision_content: Optional[List[Dict[str, Any]]] = config.get("vision_content")

        # Iterative tool loop: keep streaming completions until the model
        # produces a final answer (no more tool_calls finish reason).
        while True:
            # Stop BEFORE spending more when the chat already reached its
            # estimated cost (covers the case where a previous round pushed the
            # chat over budget).
            if self._cost_limit_exceeded(current_chat, chat_cost):
                cost_limit_error = ESTIMATION_COST_EXCEEDED_MSG.format(
                    spent=chat_cost,
                    limit=current_chat.estimation_cost,
                )
                logger.warning(
                    "SmolAgent: chat cost limit reached before round %d "
                    "(spent=%.4f, limit=%.4f); stopping gracefully",
                    loop_guard.rounds + 1,
                    chat_cost,
                    current_chat.estimation_cost,
                )
                break

            request_id = str(uuid.uuid4())
            content, tool_calls, usage_info = await self._stream_completion(
                kwargs=kwargs,
                openai_messages=openai_messages,
                headers=headers,
                cancellation_token=cancellation_token,
                send_callback=send_callback,
                run_context=run_context,
                request_id=request_id,
                chat_id=chat_id,
                system_message=system_message,
                vision_content=vision_content,
            )

            # Register the cost of this round (iteration) in cxjcoins and add
            # it to both the iteration total and the chat total.
            round_cost = self._compute_cost(
                usage_info=usage_info,
                content=content,
                openai_messages=openai_messages,
            )
            iteration_cost += round_cost.total_cost_cxjcoins
            chat_cost += round_cost.total_cost_cxjcoins
            total_input_tokens += round_cost.input_tokens
            total_output_tokens += round_cost.output_tokens
            total_input_cost += round_cost.input_cost_cxjcoins
            total_output_cost += round_cost.output_cost_cxjcoins
            logger.info(
                "SmolAgent: round cost %.6f cxjcoins "
                "(iteration total %.6f, chat total %.6f)",
                round_cost.total_cost_cxjcoins,
                iteration_cost,
                chat_cost,
            )

            if not tool_calls:
                # Final response (no tool calls): accumulate in final_answer_content
                # and exit the loop.
                if content:
                    final_answer_content += content
                break

            # Enforce the chat cost budget BEFORE executing more tools so the
            # chat does not spend beyond the estimated cost the user set.
            if self._cost_limit_exceeded(current_chat, chat_cost):
                cost_limit_error = ESTIMATION_COST_EXCEEDED_MSG.format(
                    spent=chat_cost,
                    limit=current_chat.estimation_cost,
                )
                logger.warning(
                    "SmolAgent: chat cost limit reached at round %d "
                    "(spent=%.4f, limit=%.4f); stopping before tools",
                    loop_guard.rounds + 1,
                    chat_cost,
                    current_chat.estimation_cost,
                )
                break

            # Tool calls detected: mark that tools were used and accumulate LLM
            # text in thinking_content (this is preprocessing/reasoning).
            tools_were_used = True
            if content:
                thinking_content += content
                logger.debug(
                    "SmolAgent: round %d accumulated %d bytes of LLM text "
                    "before tool execution",
                    loop_guard.rounds + 1,
                    len(content),
                )

            # Separate cached and non-cached tool calls
            cached_calls: Dict[str, Dict[str, Any]] = {}
            uncached_calls: Dict[str, Dict[str, Any]] = {}

            for tool_id, tool_call in tool_calls.items():
                func_name = tool_call["function"]
                params = self._parse_tool_arguments(
                    tool_call.get("arguments"), func_name
                )
                cached_result = tool_cache.get(func_name, params)

                if cached_result is not None:
                    cached_calls[tool_id] = {
                        "tool_call": tool_call,
                        "params": params,
                        "result": cached_result,
                    }
                else:
                    uncached_calls[tool_id] = tool_call

            # Guard ONLY against uncached tool calls. Cached results bypass
            # LoopGuard checks entirely (don't count towards max_tool_calls
            # or max_iterations).
            if uncached_calls:
                try:
                    loop_guard.check(uncached_calls)
                except ToolLoopError as ex:
                    # Limits reached: do NOT let the exception abort the run
                    # (that would discard every tool result gathered so far).
                    # Stop the loop and summarise the tools used so the work
                    # survives in the response message and can be reused in the
                    # next iteration without re-executing the same tools.
                    loop_limit_error = str(ex)
                    logger.warning(
                        "SmolAgent: tool loop limit reached at round %d (%s); "
                        "stopping gracefully and summarising tool usage",
                        loop_guard.rounds,
                        loop_limit_error,
                    )
                    break

            total_tools = len(tool_calls)
            cached_count = len(cached_calls)
            if cached_count > 0:
                logger.info(
                    "SmolAgent: round %d: %d/%d tool(s) cached, "
                    "%d new",
                    loop_guard.rounds,
                    cached_count,
                    total_tools,
                    len(uncached_calls),
                )

            logger.info(
                "SmolAgent: round %d: executing %d tool(s)",
                loop_guard.rounds,
                len(uncached_calls),
            )

            # Add message to record which tools were requested
            openai_messages.append(
                make_assistant_tool_calls_message(tool_calls, content=content)
            )

            # Process cached tool calls (no execution, just emit events)
            for tool_id, cached_info in cached_calls.items():
                tool_call = cached_info["tool_call"]
                result = cached_info["result"]
                func_name = tool_call["function"]

                # Emit TOOL_END with cached=True for observability
                run_context.emit(
                    AgentEventType.TOOL_END,
                    tool=func_name,
                    tool_call_id=tool_id,
                    duration_ms=0,
                    result=(
                        result[:TOOL_RESULT_PREVIEW_MAX_CHARS]
                        if isinstance(result, str)
                        else str(result)[:TOOL_RESULT_PREVIEW_MAX_CHARS]
                    ),
                    cached=True,
                )

                # Emit tool logs if ToolResponse has any
                if isinstance(result, ToolResponse) and result.logs:
                    run_context.emit(
                        AgentEventType.TOOL_LOGS,
                        tool=func_name,
                        tool_call_id=tool_id,
                        logs=result.logs,
                    )

                # Tool output is NOT merged into the chat content anymore: it is
                # delivered as a collapsible message property
                # (``ResponseMessage.tool_events[].output``) via the TOOL_END
                # event emitted when the tool actually executed. Cache hits only
                # reuse the tool result sent to the model, so no output is
                # re-emitted here (avoids duplicating the same output block).
                if isinstance(result, ToolResponse):
                    llm_response = _normalise_tool_result(
                        result.llm_response, func_name
                    )
                    openai_messages.append(
                        make_tool_message(
                            tool_call_id=tool_id,
                            content=llm_response,
                        )
                    )
                else:
                    # Plain cached result: send to model only
                    openai_messages.append(
                        make_tool_message(
                            tool_call_id=tool_id,
                            content=_normalise_tool_result(result, func_name),
                        )
                    )

                logger.debug(
                    "SmolAgent: cached tool '%s' appended to conversation "
                    "(openai_messages now has %d entries)",
                    func_name,
                    len(openai_messages),
                )

            # Process uncached tool calls — check cancellation between each
            # tool execution so a cancellation request is honoured promptly
            # even when multiple tools are being processed sequentially in
            # one round.
            for tool_id, tool_call in uncached_calls.items():
                # Cancellation checkpoint BEFORE each tool.
                # _execute_tool also calls checkpoint internally, but checking
                # here ensures we never start a tool when already cancelled.
                run_context.checkpoint()

                tool_result = await self._execute_tool(
                    tool_call,
                    request_id=request_id,
                    chat_id=chat_id,
                    run_context=run_context,
                    tool_cache=tool_cache,
                )

                if isinstance(tool_result, ToolResponse):
                    # Dual-response tool:
                    # - user_response → delivered as a collapsible message
                    #   property (``ResponseMessage.tool_events[].output``) via
                    #   the TOOL_END event emitted by ``_execute_tool``; it is
                    #   NOT merged into the chat content.
                    # - llm_response → model tool message only (NOT in response)
                    # Normalise LLM feedback – the model must never receive
                    # an empty tool message or it will repeat the same call.
                    llm_response = _normalise_tool_result(
                        tool_result.llm_response, tool_call["function"]
                    )
                    openai_messages.append(
                        make_tool_message(
                            tool_call_id=tool_id,
                            content=llm_response,
                        )
                    )
                else:
                    # Traditional single-response tool: normalise and send to
                    # the model only. Plain tool results are NOT added to any
                    # response (thinking, final or tool output).
                    normalised = _normalise_tool_result(
                        tool_result, tool_call["function"]
                    )
                    openai_messages.append(
                        make_tool_message(
                            tool_call_id=tool_id,
                            content=normalised,
                        )
                    )

                # Register any cost reported by the tool itself (e.g. a tool
                # that performs its own AI call) into this iteration and the
                # chat total, so it is billed on the response message and
                # counted towards the estimation_cost budget. Cached results
                # are intentionally skipped: no new cost is incurred when a
                # tool result is reused within the same run.
                tool_cost = self._tool_cost(tool_result)
                if tool_cost:
                    iteration_cost += tool_cost
                    chat_cost += tool_cost
                    total_tool_cost += tool_cost
                    tool_cost_by_name[tool_call["function"]] = (
                        tool_cost_by_name.get(tool_call["function"], 0.0)
                        + tool_cost
                    )
                    logger.info(
                        "SmolAgent: tool '%s' reported cost %.6f cxjcoins "
                        "(iteration total %.6f, chat total %.6f)",
                        tool_call["function"],
                        tool_cost,
                        iteration_cost,
                        chat_cost,
                    )

                logger.debug(
                    "SmolAgent: tool '%s' appended to conversation "
                    "(openai_messages now has %d entries)",
                    tool_call["function"],
                    len(openai_messages),
                )

            # FIX 1: INCREMENT LOOP GUARD AFTER PROCESSING ALL TOOLS
            # This is CRITICAL for preventing infinite loops when:
            # 1. All tool calls are cached (normally bypass loop guard checks)
            # 2. Model requests same tool repeatedly with identical args
            # 3. Vision content or attachments trigger repeated tool calls
            #
            # Incrementing here ensures:
            # - loop_guard.rounds increases every iteration (even all-cached)
            # - Stuck loop detection works for cached tool repetition
            # - max_iterations limit is enforced regardless of cache hits
            if tool_calls:
                loop_guard.rounds += 1
                logger.info(
                    "SmolAgent: round %d complete (cached=%d, uncached=%d, "
                    "iterations_left=%d/%d)",
                    loop_guard.rounds,
                    cached_count,
                    len(uncached_calls),
                    loop_guard.max_iterations - loop_guard.rounds if loop_guard.max_iterations else "unlimited",
                    loop_guard.max_iterations if loop_guard.max_iterations else "unlimited",
                )

        duration_seconds = time.monotonic() - request_start
        self._record_usage(
            openai_messages=openai_messages,
            output_text=final_answer_content,
            thinking_text=thinking_content if tools_were_used else "",
            duration_seconds=duration_seconds,
            tags=tags,
            session_id=session_id,
            request_id=request_id,
            usage_info=usage_info,
            chat_id=chat_id,
            tool_cache=tool_cache,
        )

        # When the run was stopped by LoopGuard, append a summary of the tools
        # used (findings + useless calls) produced by the knowledge/RAG model.
        # This preserves the tool context in the response message so the next
        # iteration can continue without re-executing the same tools, and gives

"""
SmolAgent: a small, async-only OpenAI chat agent.

Compared to the removed :class:`codx.junior.ai.openai_ai.OpenAI_AI`, this
implementation:
    * exposes a single async ``chat()`` method (no sync variant),
    * uses an **iterative** tool loop instead of recursion,
    * delegates loop protection to :class:`LoopGuard`,
    * delegates logging, event emission and cancellation to
      :class:`engine.agent_runtime.AgentRunContext`,
    * keeps streaming, callbacks, cancellation and analytics.
    * caches tool results per conversation to avoid re-execution.
    * returns a typed :class:`AgentRunResult` (no untyped ``additional_kwargs``).

Tool events (``TOOL_START`` / ``TOOL_END`` / ``TOOL_ERROR`` / ``TOOL_LOGS``) carry the
``tool_call_id``, the parsed JSON request args and a truncated result preview
so listeners (e.g. the ChatEventBridge) can surface tool executions as chat
messages in real time. ``TOOL_END`` additionally carries the dual-response tool's
user-facing ``output`` (see Message Structure below). Tool logs are emitted for
forensic audit trail.

Loop-Limit Handling
When :class:`LoopGuard` stops the run (max rounds, max tool calls or stuck
loop), the run is **not** aborted. Instead the tool-usage value is summarised
by the project's knowledge/RAG model and appended to the assistant answer, so
the findings survive in the persisted message and the next iteration can
continue without re-running the same tools. The summary request is
best-effort, does not count towards the loop limits, and its token usage is
recorded separately with the ``tool-analysis`` tag.

Cost-Limit Handling
Every round (iteration) computes its cost in cxjcoins from the provider usage
and the model price settings, accumulates it into the chat total and reports it
on the returned :class:`AgentRunResult` (``result.cost``). Tools that report
their own cost through :attr:`ToolResponse.cost` are summed into both the
per-run total and the chat total. The chat total is seeded from ``Chat.cost``
(the accumulated, deletion-safe value maintained by ChatManager) so the budget
applies to the whole chat and is not reset when messages are deleted. When the
chat reaches its estimated cost (``Chat.estimation_cost``), the run stops
gracefully — before executing further tools — to keep the chat within budget.

Message Structure
A single final assistant message is always produced. Its ``content`` holds only
the model's own text: reasoning emitted between tool rounds plus the final
answer. Tool output is NO LONGER merged into the message content. For
dual-response tools, ``ToolResponse.user_response`` is emitted on the ``TOOL_END``
event and attached to the response message as a collapsible property
(``ToolEvent.output``), so the client decides how to render it (collapsed or
hidden) and the chat stays clean.

Binary files (PDFs, images) are passed as vision content when models support it.
The content is merged into the final user message to enable vision-capable models
to process images and documents alongside text.

Error Visibility
Every AI provider interaction (the completion request, the streaming of its
response and the tool-usage summary request) is guarded so failures are logged

## Why `PROFILE_LEARNING_TOOL_NAME` is removed from `ProfileManager`

Because **the agent injects the tools now, and it is the only place that can do it correctly**:

1. **Injection is per-run and permission-aware.** `ProfileManager` composes a profile for a *project*; it has no user, no chat and no run context, so it cannot know whether the caller may learn (project admin, `knowledge_admin` or codx-junior admin). Appending `profile_learning` there handed a write-capable tool to *every* user on *every* profile, and the only guard left was inside the tool — the model would see and try a tool it was not allowed to use.
2. **Two different scopes.** `profile_knowledge_search` (read) is needed whenever profiles take part in the turn; `profile_learning` (write) only for knowledge admins. `Profile.tools` is a single static list, it cannot express "depends on who is asking".
3. **No persistence/round-trip problems.** With the tools out of `Profile.tools`, `save_profile` no longer needs to strip them before writing the `.profile` JSON, and the UI editing a profile can never freeze an implicit tool into the definition.

import os
import json
import pathlib
import logging
import re
import shutil

from datetime import datetime
from typing import Any, Dict, List, Optional, Set

from codx.junior.settings import CODXJuniorSettings
from codx.junior.model.model import Profile
from codx.junior.utils.utils import write_file

from codx.junior.project.project_discover import (
    find_project_parents,
    find_project_by_name
)

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Project enrichment & profile knowledge
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# A project can enrich a profile it does not own without editing the profile
# itself, through two per-project resources stored next to the profile folder:
#
#   <project .codx>/profiles/<Name>/enrich.md        -> extra instructions
#   <project .codx>/profiles/<Name>/knowledge/**     -> reference files
#
# The base (built-in) profile keeps its knowledge in
# `codx/junior/profiles/<Name>/knowledge/**`.
#
# Both resources are additive and optional: no file, no folder => the profile
# behaves exactly as before.
#
# NOTE: profile tools (`profile_learning`, `profile_knowledge_search`) are NOT
# handled here. They depend on the user and on the chat turn, so the agent
# (SmolAgent) decides whether to inject them into each request.
ENRICH_FILE_NAME = "enrich.md"
KNOWLEDGE_FOLDER_NAME = "knowledge"

# Enriched content is wrapped in invisible markers so `save_profile` can strip
# it back out: a composed content must never be persisted as the profile's own
# content.
ENRICH_BLOCK_PATTERN = re.compile(
    r"<!--\s*codx:enrich[^>]*-->.*?<!--\s*/codx:enrich\s*-->",
    re.DOTALL | re.IGNORECASE,
)

# Knowledge files are plain text resources: everything else is ignored so the
# tool never returns binary blobs.
TEXT_KNOWLEDGE_EXTENSIONS = {
    ".md", ".markdown", ".txt", ".rst",
    ".json", ".yaml", ".yml", ".csv", ".toml",
}

# Guardrail for reading: a knowledge file is injected into the model context.
MAX_KNOWLEDGE_FILE_SIZE = 512 * 1024

# Lines of context around a search hit.
EXCERPT_CONTEXT_LINES = 4


def strip_profile_enrichment(content: str) -> str:
    """
    Remove every project enrichment block from a (possibly composed) content.

    :param content: Profile content, with or without enrichment blocks.
    :return: The content without enrichment blocks (the profile's own text).
    """
    return ENRICH_BLOCK_PATTERN.sub("", content or "").strip("\n")


def generate_llm_tree(root_path, indent="", is_last=True, ignore_list=None):
    if ignore_list is None:
        ignore_list = {'.git', '__pycache__', '.vscode', '.DS_Store', 'node_modules', 'venv'}
    
    path = pathlib.Path(root_path)
    if not path.exists():
        return "Invalid Path"

    # Header for the root on the first call
    tree_str = f"{indent}{'└── ' if is_last else '├── '}{path.name}/\n"
    
    # Update indent for children
    new_indent = indent + ("    " if is_last else "│   ")
    
    # Filter and sort items (directories first, then files)
    items = [i for i in path.iterdir() if i.name not in ignore_list]
    items.sort(key=lambda x: (not x.is_dir(), x.name.lower()))
    
    for i, item in enumerate(items):
        last_item = (i == len(items) - 1)
        if item.is_dir():
            tree_str += generate_llm_tree(item, new_indent, last_item, ignore_list)
        #else:
        #    connector = "└── " if last_item else "├── "
        #    tree_str += f"{new_indent}{connector}{item.name}\n"
            
    return tree_str

class ProfileManager:
    def __init__(self, settings: CODXJuniorSettings):
        self.settings = settings
        self.profiles_path = f"{settings.codx_path}/profiles"
        os.makedirs(self.profiles_path, exist_ok=True)

        current_file_path = os.path.abspath(__file__)
        current_directory = os.path.dirname(current_file_path)
        self.base_profiles_path = f"{current_directory}"

        # Cache of the project inheritance chain (parents -> this project)
        self._profile_chain_cache: Optional[List["ProfileManager"]] = None

    def base_profiles(self):
        def _files (file_gen):
            return [str(file) for file in file_gen]

        base_profiles = _files(pathlib.Path(self.base_profiles_path).rglob("**/*.profile"))
        return _files(base_profiles)

    def project_profile_paths(self):
        def _files (file_gen):
            return [str(file) for file in file_gen]

        # Look for profiles in both old format (flat) and new format (in folders)
        profiles = []
        # New format: [profile_name]/[profile_name].profile
        profiles.extend(_files(list(pathlib.Path(self.profiles_path).rglob("*/*.profile"))))
        # Old format fallback: *.profile (for backward compatibility)
        profiles.extend(_files(list(pathlib.Path(self.profiles_path).glob("*.profile"))))
        
        return profiles

    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Profile inheritance chain (project -> parents -> codx-junior)
    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    def profile_chain(self) -> List["ProfileManager"]:
        """
        Return the profile managers of this project's inheritance chain.

        Order: outermost parent first, then every intermediate project, and
        this project last (the most specific level). ``codx-junior`` is added as
        a regular level, exactly like :meth:`list_all_profiles` does, and
        duplicates are dropped.

        The chain is cached per instance: composing a profile reads it on every
        read path (list, read, chat composition).

        :return: ProfileManagers, outermost parent -> this project.
        """
        if self._profile_chain_cache is not None:
            return self._profile_chain_cache

        seen_ids = {self.settings.project_id}
        chain: List["ProfileManager"] = []

        parents = list(find_project_parents(project=self.settings))
        codx_junior = find_project_by_name("codx-junior")
        if codx_junior and codx_junior.project_id not in seen_ids:
            parents.append(codx_junior)

        # Shortest path first => outermost parent first.
        parents.sort(key=lambda project: len(project.project_path or ""))

        for project in parents:
            if project.project_id in seen_ids:
                continue
            seen_ids.add(project.project_id)
            chain.append(ProfileManager(settings=project))

        chain.append(self)
        self._profile_chain_cache = chain
        return chain

    def owns_profile(self, profile_name: str) -> bool:
        """
        Return True when THIS level defines the profile (a new line).

        A level defining ``<Name>.profile`` owns the profile: it does not
        inherit the enrichment of the levels above it.

        :param profile_name: Profile name.
        :return: True when the profile is defined at this level.
        """
        if not profile_name:
            return False
        folder_profile = os.path.join(
            self.profiles_path, profile_name, f"{profile_name}.profile"
        )
        flat_profile = os.path.join(self.profiles_path, f"{profile_name}.profile")
        return os.path.isfile(folder_profile) or os.path.isfile(flat_profile)

    def profile_exists(self, profile_name: str) -> bool:
        """
        Return True when the profile is visible from this project.

        :param profile_name: Profile name.
        :return: True for project, inherited or built-in profiles.
        """
        if not profile_name:
            return False
        if os.path.isfile(
            os.path.join(self.base_profiles_path, f"{profile_name}.profile")
        ):
            return True
        return any(manager.owns_profile(profile_name) for manager in self.profile_chain())

    def profile_enrich_path(self, profile_name: str) -> str:
        """
        Path of the enrichment file of a profile at THIS level.

        It lives inside the profile folder (``<Name>/enrich.md``), so it can
        never be confused with the profile's own content (``<Name>/<Name>.md``).

        :param profile_name: Profile name.
        :return: Absolute path to the enrichment markdown file.
        """
        return os.path.join(self.profiles_path, profile_name, ENRICH_FILE_NAME)

    def profile_knowledge_path(self, profile_name: str) -> str:
        """
        Knowledge folder of a profile at THIS level.

        :param profile_name: Profile name.
        :return: Absolute path to ``<profiles>/<Name>/knowledge``.
        """
        return os.path.join(
            self.profiles_path, profile_name, KNOWLEDGE_FOLDER_NAME
        )

    def base_profile_knowledge_path(self, profile_name: str) -> str:
        """
        Knowledge folder of the built-in (base) profile.

        :param profile_name: Profile name.
        :return: Absolute path to ``codx/junior/profiles/<Name>/knowledge``.
        """
        return os.path.join(
            self.base_profiles_path, profile_name, KNOWLEDGE_FOLDER_NAME
        )

    @staticmethod
    def _read_text(path: str, max_size: int = MAX_KNOWLEDGE_FILE_SIZE) -> str:
        """
        Read a text file, returning an empty string when it cannot be used.

        :param path: File path.
        :param max_size: Files bigger than this are skipped.
        :return: File content (empty string on error or when missing).
        """
        try:
            if not os.path.isfile(path):
                return ""
            if os.path.getsize(path) > max_size:
                logger.warning("Skipping oversized profile resource: %s", path)
                return ""
            with open(path, "r", encoding="utf-8", errors="ignore") as f:
                return f.read()
        except Exception as ex:
            logger.warning("Could not read profile resource '%s': %s", path, ex)
            return ""

    @staticmethod
    def _wrap_enrichment(project_name: str, text: str) -> str:
        """
        Wrap enrichment text in the markers used to strip it on save.

        :param project_name: Project the enrichment comes from.
        :param text: Enrichment markdown.
        :return: Marked block.
        """
        return "\n".join([
            f"<!-- codx:enrich project={project_name or 'project'} -->",
            text.strip("\n"),
            "<!-- /codx:enrich -->",
        ])

    def compose_profile_content(self, profile: Profile) -> str:
        """
        Build the effective content of a profile for THIS project.

        Composition = the profile's own content + the enrichment of every level
        between the level that owns the profile and this project (outermost
        first). A level that defines the profile starts a new line, so it never
        receives enrichment from above.

        When no level has an enrichment file, the content is returned untouched.

        :param profile: Profile loaded by :meth:`load_profile` (own content).
        :return: Composed content (own content when there is no enrichment).
        """
        if not profile or not profile.name:
            return profile.content or ""

        own_content = (profile.content or "").strip("\n")

        chain = self.profile_chain()
        owner_index = -1
        for index, manager in enumerate(chain):
            if manager.owns_profile(profile.name):
                owner_index = index

        blocks: List[str] = []
        for manager in chain[owner_index + 1:]:
            enrich_path = manager.profile_enrich_path(profile.name)
            text = self._read_text(enrich_path).strip("\n")
            if not text:
                continue
            blocks.append(self._wrap_enrichment(manager.settings.project_name, text))

        if not blocks:
            return profile.content or ""

        parts = ([own_content] if own_content else []) + blocks
        return "\n\n".join(parts)

    def list_all_profiles(self):
        parent_projects = find_project_parents(project=self.settings)
        codx_junior = find_project_by_name("codx-junior")
        if codx_junior:
            parent_projects.append(codx_junior)
        logger.info("list_all_profiles: %s", [p.project_name for p in parent_projects])
        
        all_profiles = {}
        
        # 1. Parent and codx-junior project profiles
        for project in parent_projects:
            profiles = ProfileManager(settings=project).list_profiles()
            for profile in profiles:
                all_profiles[profile.name] = profile
        
        # 2. Current project profiles (can override parent profiles)
        for profile in self.list_profiles():
            all_profiles[profile.name] = profile

        # 3. Built-in base profiles from source code (only if not already defined)
        for profile_path in self.base_profiles():
            profile = self.load_profile(profile_path)
            if profile and profile.name not in all_profiles:
                all_profiles[profile.name] = profile
        
        return [self.get_profile_With_content(profile=p) for p in list(all_profiles.values())]


    def list_profiles(self):
        profiles = [self.load_profile(profile_path) for profile_path in self.project_profile_paths()]
        return [p for p in profiles if p is not None]

    def read_profile(self, profile_name) -> Profile:
        project_profile_paths = self.project_profile_paths()
        match_profiles = [profile_path for profile_path in project_profile_paths if profile_name in profile_path]
        if not match_profiles:
            return None
        profile = self.load_profile(match_profiles[0])
        # Composed content: callers never need to know about project enrichment.
        return self.get_profile_With_content(profile=profile) if profile else None

    def load_profile(self, profile_path) -> Profile:
        """
        Load a profile from disk returning its OWN content (no enrichment).

        This is the private building block: :meth:`read_profile` and
        :meth:`get_profile_With_content` compose the project enrichment on top.

        :param profile_path: Path of the ``<Name>.profile`` JSON file.
        :return: The loaded profile (or a minimal valid one on error).
        """
        profile = None
        try:
            with open(profile_path, 'r') as f:
                content = f.read()
                
                # Validate content is not empty
                if not content or not content.strip():
                    logger.warning(f"Profile file is empty, using defaults: {profile_path}")
                    profile = Profile(name=pathlib.Path(profile_path).stem)
                else:
                    try:
                        profile = Profile(**json.loads(content))
                    except json.JSONDecodeError as json_ex:
                        logger.error(f"Invalid JSON in profile {profile_path}: {json_ex}. Using defaults.")
                        profile = Profile(name=pathlib.Path(profile_path).stem)
                
                profile.path = profile_path

            # Load content from markdown file in new format: [profile_name]/[profile_name].md
            profile_dir = os.path.dirname(profile_path)
            markdown_content_path = os.path.join(profile_dir, f"{profile.name}.md")
            
            if os.path.isfile(markdown_content_path):
                with open(markdown_content_path, 'r') as f:
                    profile.content = f.read()
                # logger.info(f"Loaded profile content from: {markdown_content_path}")
            
            if not profile.avatar:
                profile.avatar = f"https://gravatar.com/avatar/baa8db8ab2afb7ababc235269e762662?s=400&d=robohash&r={profile.name}"
            profile.project_id = self.settings.project_id
            return profile
        except Exception as ex:
            logger.exception(f"Error loading profile: {profile_path} {ex}")
            # Return a minimal valid profile instead of raising
            return Profile(
                name=pathlib.Path(profile_path).stem,
                path=profile_path,
                project_id=self.settings.project_id,
                avatar=f"https://gravatar.com/avatar/baa8db8ab2afb7ababc235269e762662?s=400&d=robohash&r={pathlib.Path(profile_path).stem}"
            )

    def _migrate_profile_to_folder(self, profile_name: str, old_profile_path: str):
        """Migrate a profile from flat structure to folder structure"""
        profile_folder = os.path.join(self.profiles_path, profile_name)
        os.makedirs(profile_folder, exist_ok=True)
        
        new_profile_path = os.path.join(profile_folder, f"{profile_name}.profile")
        
        # Move profile JSON file
        if os.path.isfile(old_profile_path) and old_profile_path != new_profile_path:
            shutil.move(old_profile_path, new_profile_path)
            logger.info(f"Migrated profile from {old_profile_path} to {new_profile_path}")
        
        # Move associated markdown content file (old format: [profile_name].md.profile or [profile_name].profile.md)
        old_markdown_paths = [
            f"{old_profile_path.replace('.profile', '')}.md.profile",
            f"{old_profile_path.replace('.profile', '')}.profile.md"
        ]
        
        for old_markdown_path in old_markdown_paths:
            if os.path.isfile(old_markdown_path):
                new_markdown_path = os.path.join(profile_folder, f"{profile_name}.md")
                shutil.move(old_markdown_path, new_markdown_path)
                logger.info(f"Migrated markdown content from {old_markdown_path} to {new_markdown_path}")
                break

    def save_profile(self, profile: Profile):
        if not profile.name:
            raise Exception('Invalid profile')

        # Create profile folder
        profile_folder = os.path.join(self.profiles_path, profile.name)
        os.makedirs(profile_folder, exist_ok=True)
        
        # New profile path in folder structure
        profile_path = os.path.join(profile_folder, f"{profile.name}.profile")
        
        logger.info(f"Save profile {profile_path}")
        
        # Check if profile exists in old flat format and migrate it
        old_profile_path = os.path.join(self.profiles_path, f"{profile.name}.profile")
        if os.path.isfile(old_profile_path) and old_profile_path != profile_path:
            self._migrate_profile_to_folder(profile.name, old_profile_path)
        
        # Save profile content to markdown file in new format: [profile_name]/[profile_name].md
        # The project enrichment blocks are never persisted: the content written
        # is always the profile's own content.
        if profile.content:
            markdown_content_path = os.path.join(profile_folder, f"{profile.name}.md")
            with open(markdown_content_path, 'w') as f:
                f.write(strip_profile_enrichment(profile.content))
            logger.info(f"Saved profile content to: {markdown_content_path}")
        
        # Save profile JSON without content property
        with open(profile_path, 'w') as f:
            profile_data = profile.model_dump()
            profile_data['content'] = None
            profile_data['parsed_content'] = None
            f.write(json.dumps(profile_data, indent=2))

    def delete_profile(self, profile_name):
        # Delete profile in new folder structure
        profile_folder = os.path.join(self.profiles_path, profile_name)
        if os.path.isdir(profile_folder):
            shutil.rmtree(profile_folder)
            logger.info(f"Deleted profile folder: {profile_folder}")
        
        # Also check and delete old flat format (backward compatibility)
        old_profile_path = os.path.join(self.profiles_path, f"{profile_name}.profile")
        if os.path.isfile(old_profile_path):
            os.remove(old_profile_path)
            logger.info(f"Deleted old format profile: {old_profile_path}")
            
            old_markdown_paths = [
                f"{old_profile_path.replace('.profile', '')}.md.profile",
                f"{old_profile_path.replace('.profile', '')}.profile.md"
            ]
            for old_markdown_path in old_markdown_paths:
                if os.path.isfile(old_markdown_path):
                    os.remove(old_markdown_path)
                    logger.info(f"Deleted old format markdown: {old_markdown_path}")

    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Profile learning: extra instructions (rules) and knowledge files
    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    def add_profile_instructions(
        self,
        profile_name: str,
        text: str,
        title: Optional[str] = None
    ) -> str:
        """
        Append a rule ("hardcoded" extra content) to this project's profile.

        The text is written to ``<profiles>/<Name>/enrich.md`` and composed into
        the profile content from the next read on, for this project and its
        children (unless a child defines the profile itself).

        :param profile_name: Profile being enriched.
        :param text: Markdown instructions to remember.
        :param title: Optional heading for the new block.
        :return: Path of the enrichment file.
        """
        profile_name = (profile_name or "").strip()
        text = (text or "").strip()
        if not profile_name:
            raise ValueError("profile_name is required")
        if not text:
            raise ValueError("content is required: write the instructions to remember")
        if not self.profile_exists(profile_name):
            raise ValueError(
                f"Unknown profile '{profile_name}': it does not exist in this "
                "project, in a parent project or in the base profiles."
            )

        enrich_path = self.profile_enrich_path(profile_name)
        os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(enrich_path), exist_ok=True)

        existing = self._read_text(enrich_path).rstrip("\n")
        heading = (title or "").strip() or f"Learned instructions ({datetime.now():%Y-%m-%d})"
        block = f"## {heading}\n\n{text}"
        content = f"{existing}\n\n{block}".strip("\n") + "\n" if existing else block + "\n"

        with open(enrich_path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
            f.write(content)

        logger.info(
            "Profile '%s' learned new instructions in project '%s' (%s)",
            profile_name,
            self.settings.project_name,
            enrich_path,
        )
        return enrich_path

    def profile_knowledge_roots(self, profile_name: str) -> List[Dict[str, str]]:
        """
        Resolve every knowledge folder visible for a profile, in chain order.

        Order: built-in base, then the project levels from the outermost parent
        down to this project. Missing folders are skipped.

        :param profile_name: Profile name.
        :return: List of ``{"source", "path"}`` dicts.
        """
        if not profile_name:
            return []

        roots: List[Dict[str, str]] = [{
            "source": "base",
            "path": self.base_profile_knowledge_path(profile_name),
        }]
        for manager in self.profile_chain():
            roots.append({
                "source": manager.settings.project_name or "project",
                "path": manager.profile_knowledge_path(profile_name),
            })
        return [root for root in roots if os.path.isdir(root["path"])]

    def list_profile_knowledge(self, profile_name: str) -> List[Dict[str, Any]]:
        """
        List the text knowledge files available for a profile.

        :param profile_name: Profile name.
        :return: List of ``{source, path, file, size}`` dicts.
        """
        files: List[Dict[str, Any]] = []
        for root in self.profile_knowledge_roots(profile_name):
            for file_path in sorted(pathlib.Path(root["path"]).rglob("*")):
                if not file_path.is_file():
                    continue
                if file_path.suffix.lower() not in TEXT_KNOWLEDGE_EXTENSIONS:
                    continue
                files.append({
                    "source": root["source"],
                    "path": str(file_path),
                    "file": os.path.relpath(str(file_path), root["path"]),
                    "size": file_path.stat().st_size,
                })
        return files

    def _resolve_knowledge_file(
        self,
        profile_name: str,
        file_name: str
    ) -> Optional[Dict[str, Any]]:
        """
        Find a knowledge file by its relative path within its knowledge folder.

        :param profile_name: Profile name.
        :param file_name: Path relative to the knowledge folder.
        :return: The matching entry, or None.
        """
        wanted = (file_name or "").strip().replace("\\", "/").lstrip("/")
        if not wanted:
            return None
        for entry in self.list_profile_knowledge(profile_name):
            if entry["file"].replace("\\", "/") == wanted:
                return entry
        return None

    def read_profile_knowledge(self, profile_name: str, file_name: str) -> str:
        """
        Read one knowledge file of a profile (base or any project level).

        :param profile_name: Profile name.
        :param file_name: Path relative to the knowledge folder.
        :return: File content.

        :raises ValueError: If the file is not found.
        """
        entry = self._resolve_knowledge_file(profile_name, file_name)
        if not entry:
            raise ValueError(
                f"Knowledge file '{file_name}' not found for profile "
                f"'{profile_name}'."
            )
        return self._read_text(entry["path"])

    def save_profile_knowledge(
        self,
        profile_name: str,
        file_name: str,
        content: str,
        overwrite: bool = False
    ) -> str:
        """
        Create or update a knowledge file for a profile in THIS project.

        Knowledge always lands in the current project, so a project can keep its
        own reference material without touching the base profile.

        :param profile_name: Profile name.
        :param file_name: Path relative to the knowledge folder.
        :param content: File content.
        :param overwrite: Replace the file when it already exists.
        :return: Path of the written file.

        :raises ValueError: On invalid input or unexpected overwrite.
        """
        profile_name = (profile_name or "").strip()
        if not profile_name:
            raise ValueError("profile_name is required")
        if not self.profile_exists(profile_name):
            raise ValueError(f"Unknown profile '{profile_name}'.")
        if content is None or not str(content).strip():
            raise ValueError("content is required")

        relative_path = self._validate_knowledge_file_name(file_name)
        knowledge_path = self.profile_knowledge_path(profile_name)
        target_path = os.path.join(knowledge_path, relative_path)

        if os.path.isfile(target_path) and not overwrite:
            raise ValueError(
                f"Knowledge file '{relative_path}' already exists for profile "
                f"'{profile_name}'. Read it first and use overwrite=True to "
                "replace it."
            )

        os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(target_path), exist_ok=True)
        with open(target_path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
            f.write(str(content))

        logger.info(
            "Profile '%s' knowledge saved by project '%s': %s",
            profile_name,
            self.settings.project_name,
            target_path,
        )
        return target_path

    def delete_profile_knowledge(self, profile_name: str, file_name: str) -> str:
        """
        Delete a knowledge file of THIS project's profile knowledge folder.

        Base and parent knowledge folders are read-only: only the current
        project's files can be deleted.

        :param profile_name: Profile name.
        :param file_name: Path relative to the knowledge folder.
        :return: Path of the deleted file.

        :raises ValueError: If the file is not owned by this project.
        """
        relative_path = self._validate_knowledge_file_name(file_name)
        knowledge_path = self.profile_knowledge_path(profile_name)
        target_path = os.path.join(knowledge_path, relative_path)

        if not os.path.isfile(target_path):
            raise ValueError(
                f"Knowledge file '{relative_path}' does not exist in this "
                f"project for profile '{profile_name}'. Base and parent "
                "knowledge files are read-only."
            )

        os.remove(target_path)
        logger.info(
            "Profile '%s' knowledge deleted: %s", profile_name, target_path
        )
        return target_path

    @staticmethod
    def _validate_knowledge_file_name(file_name: str) -> str:
        """
        Validate a knowledge file name (relative, text extension only).

        :param file_name: Candidate relative path.
        :return: Validated relative path (``.md`` added when missing).

        :raises ValueError: If the path escapes the knowledge folder or the
            extension is not a text one.
        """
        name = (file_name or "").strip().replace("\\", "/").lstrip("/")
        if not name:
            raise ValueError("file_name is required")
        if ".." in name.split("/"):
            raise ValueError(f"file_name cannot contain '..': {file_name!r}")
        if not os.path.splitext(name)[1]:
            name = f"{name}.md"
        extension = os.path.splitext(name)[1].lower()
        if extension not in TEXT_KNOWLEDGE_EXTENSIONS:
            raise ValueError(
                f"Unsupported knowledge file extension '{extension}'. Allowed: "
                f"{', '.join(sorted(TEXT_KNOWLEDGE_EXTENSIONS))}"
            )
        return name

    def search_profile_knowledge(
        self,
        profile_name: str,
        query: str,
        limit: int = 10
    ) -> List[Dict[str, Any]]:
        """
        Search the profile knowledge folders (base + every project level).

        The search is a plain case-insensitive term match on the filesystem: no
        indexing is required, so a file is searchable as soon as it is written.

        :param profile_name: Profile name.
        :param query: Search terms (whitespace separated, OR matched).
        :param limit: Maximum number of files returned.
        :return: Matching entries with ``matches`` count and an ``excerpt``.
        """
        terms = [term for term in re.split(r"\s+", (query or "").strip().lower()) if term]
        if not terms:
            raise ValueError("query is required")

        limit = max(1, min(int(limit or 10), 50))
        results: List[Dict[str, Any]] = []

        for entry in self.list_profile_knowledge(profile_name):
            text = self._read_text(entry["path"])
            if not text:
                continue
            lines = text.splitlines()
            hits = [
                index for index, line in enumerate(lines)
                if any(term in line.lower() for term in terms)
            ]
            if not hits:
                continue
            start = max(hits[0] - EXCERPT_CONTEXT_LINES, 0)
            end = min(hits[0] + EXCERPT_CONTEXT_LINES + 1, len(lines))
            results.append({
                **entry,
                "matches": len(hits),
                "excerpt": "\n".join(lines[start:end]).strip(),
            })

        results.sort(key=lambda result: result["matches"], reverse=True)
        return results[:limit]

    def is_profile_match(self, profile: Profile, file_path: str):
        try:
            return profile.file_match and re.search(profile.file_match, file_path)
        except:
            return False

    def get_file_profiles_by_file_path(self, file_path: str):
        file_profiles = [profile for profile in self.list_all_profiles() \
          if self.is_profile_match(profile=profile, file_path=file_path)]
        return self.reduce_linked_profiles(profiles=file_profiles)

    def get_profiles_by_name(self, profiles: []):
        return [p for p in self.list_all_profiles() if p.name in profiles]

    def get_profile_content_context(self, profile: Profile):
        return {
          "project_path": lambda: self.settings.abs_project_path,
          "project_name": lambda: self.settings.project_name,
          # "project_tree": lambda: generate_llm_tree(self.settings.abs_project_path)
        }

    def get_profile_With_content(self, profile: Profile):
        """
        Compose a profile for this project: own content + project enrichment.

        Every caller keeps using this method, so no other module needs to know
        that projects can enrich profiles.

        Profile tools are NOT modified here: the agent (SmolAgent) decides which
        profile tools are injected into each request, because it depends on the
        user (who may or may not be allowed to learn) and on the chat turn.

        :param profile: Profile to compose.
        :return: The same profile instance, with the composed content.
        """
        if profile:
            profile.content = self.compose_profile_content(profile)

        context = self.get_profile_content_context(profile=profile)
        
        # Regex explains:
        # {{    -> Matches literal opening braces
        # \s*   -> Matches optional whitespace
        # (\w+) -> Captures the variable name (alphanumeric/underscore)
        # \s*   -> Matches optional whitespace
        # }}    -> Matches literal closing braces
        pattern = r'\{\{\s*(\w+)\s*\}\}'

        def replacement_logic(match):
            variable_name = match.group(1)
            # Returns the value if found, otherwise keeps the original {{var}} text
            fnc = context.get(variable_name, None)
            if fnc:
                return str(fnc())
            return match.group(0)

        profile.parsed_content = re.sub(pattern, replacement_logic, profile.content or "")
        return profile

    def _profiles_by_name_registry(self) -> Dict[str, Profile]:
        """
        Build a ``name -> Profile`` index of every available profile.

        Building the index once avoids repeated (and expensive) full profile
        scans while resolving linked profile names recursively.

        :return: Mapping of profile name to profile entity (with parsed content).
        """
        return {
            profile.name: profile
            for profile in self.list_all_profiles()
            if profile and profile.name
        }

    def _expand_linked_profiles(
        self,
        profiles: List[Profile],
        seen_names: Optional[Set[str]] = None
    ) -> List[Profile]:
        """
        Expand a list of profiles with every profile they link to, recursively.

        Algorithm (one pass per profile, breadth-first):

        1. For each incoming profile we take its **name**.
        2. We find the profile entity for that name (from the registry of all
           available profiles).
        3. We read the entity's ``profiles`` property — a list of linked profile
           **names**.
        4. For every linked name we resolve the profile entity and queue it, so
           the operation repeats until no new profile is found.

        Deduplication is done by profile **name** (never by object equality),
        which makes the resolution deterministic and idempotent, and preserves
        the order in which profiles are discovered.

        :param profiles: Profiles referenced directly by the caller (the chat
                         mentions, file profiles, ...).
        :param seen_names: Optional set of already-resolved profile names,
                           shared across calls to safely ignore circular links.
        :return: The input profiles plus all their (recursively) linked profiles,
                 with no duplicates.
        """
        if seen_names is None:
            seen_names = set()

        # Resolve every linked name against this single snapshot of the
        # available profiles (avoids repeated, inconsistent disk reads).
        registry = self._profiles_by_name_registry()

        resolved: List[Profile] = []
        pending: List[Profile] = [p for p in (profiles or []) if p and p.name]

        while pending:
            profile = pending.pop(0)

            if profile.name in seen_names:
                continue
            seen_names.add(profile.name)

            # Prefer the entity loaded from the registry: it carries the
            # parsed content for use in the system prompt.
            entity = registry.get(profile.name) or profile
            resolved.append(entity)

            # Read the "profiles" property: the list of linked profile names.
            for linked_name in (entity.profiles or []):
                if not linked_name or linked_name in seen_names:
                    continue
                linked_profile = registry.get(linked_name)
                if linked_profile:
                    pending.append(linked_profile)
                else:
                    logger.warning(
                        "Profile '%s' links to unknown profile '%s'",
                        entity.name,
                        linked_name
                    )

        logger.info(
            "Expanded %d profile(s) into %d profile(s) following linked profiles: %s",
            len(profiles or []),
            len(resolved),
            [p.name for p in resolved]
        )
        return resolved

    def get_all_linked_profiles(self, profile: Profile, seen: set = None) -> List[Profile]:
        """
        Return *profile* plus every profile it links to, resolving links
        recursively by profile NAME (see :meth:`_expand_linked_profiles`).

        :param profile: The profile whose links to expand.
        :param seen: Optional set of already-resolved profile names.
        :return: The profile plus all (recursively) linked profiles.
        """
        if not profile or not profile.name:
            return []
        seen_names: Set[str] = set(seen or {})
        return self._expand_linked_profiles(profiles=[profile], seen_names=seen_names)

    def reduce_linked_profiles(self, profiles: List[Profile]) -> List[Profile]:
        """
        Expand a list of profiles with all the profiles they link to,
        recursively, and return them without duplicates.

        For each profile name we find the profile entity, read its ``profiles``
        property (a list of profile names) and, for every linked name, repeat
        the operation until all profiles are loaded.

        :param profiles: Profiles referenced directly by the caller.
        :return: The input profiles plus all their (recursively) linked profiles.
        """
        return self._expand_linked_profiles(profiles=profiles, seen_names=set())

    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Team (ADDED): profiles the LLM can use in NEW tasks
    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    @staticmethod
    def profile_short_description(profile: Profile, max_length: int = 160) -> str:
        """
        Return a short one-line description of *profile* for the team table.

        Resolution order: ``Profile.description`` → first meaningful line of the
        profile content (markdown heading markers removed) → ``Profile.category``.
        Whitespace is collapsed (the description must stay inside a table cell)
        and the result is truncated to *max_length* characters.

        :param profile: The profile to describe.
        :param max_length: Maximum length of the returned description.
        :return: Single-line description (may be an empty string).
        """
        description = (profile.description or "").strip()

        if not description and profile.content:
            for line in profile.content.splitlines():
                candidate = line.strip().lstrip("#").strip()
                if candidate:
                    description = candidate
                    break

        if not description:
            description = profile.category or ""

        # Collapse newlines and repeated spaces so the table stays a table.
        description = " ".join(description.split())

        if len(description) > max_length:
            description = description[:max_length - 3].rstrip() + "..."

        return description

    def get_team_profiles(
        self,
        profiles: List[Profile],
        exclude: Optional[List[Profile]] = None
    ) -> List[Profile]:
        """
        Resolve the TEAM of the given profiles: the profiles the LLM can use in
        NEW tasks.

        A profile declares its team through the ``team`` property — a list of
        profile **names**, like ``profiles`` lists linked profiles. Unlike
        linked profiles:

        * team members are NOT composed into the system prompt; they are only
          offered as a table (name + short description),
        * their links are NOT expanded: a team member's own team is offered only
          once that profile becomes active in a chat.

        Profiles already active in the turn (*exclude*, i.e. the profiles being
        composed) are not offered again, and unknown names are logged and
        skipped. Resolution is best effort: a broken team reference never
        blocks the chat.

        :param profiles: Profiles active in the current turn.
        :param exclude: Profiles (or profile names) that must not be offered.
        :return: Resolved team profiles, deduplicated by name, order preserved.
        """
        if not profiles:
            return []

        registry = self._profiles_by_name_registry()

        excluded_names: Set[str] = set()
        for excluded in (exclude or []):
            if isinstance(excluded, Profile):
                excluded_names.add(excluded.name)
            elif isinstance(excluded, dict):
                excluded_names.add(str(excluded.get("name") or ""))
            else:
                excluded_names.add(str(excluded).lstrip("@"))

        team_profiles: List[Profile] = []
        seen_names: Set[str] = set()

        for profile in profiles:
            for team_name in (profile.team or []):
                # Mentions may declare the member as "@name".
                team_name = (team_name or "").strip().lstrip("@")
                if not team_name or team_name in seen_names \
                        or team_name in excluded_names:
                    continue

                team_profile = registry.get(team_name)
                if not team_profile:
                    logger.warning(
                        "Profile '%s' lists unknown team profile '%s'",
                        profile.name,
                        team_name
                    )
                    continue

                seen_names.add(team_name)
                team_profiles.append(team_profile)

        logger.info(
            "Resolved team of %s: %s",
            [p.name for p in profiles],
            [p.name for p in team_profiles]
        )
        return team_profiles
