            old_markdown_paths = [
                f"{old_profile_path.replace('.profile', '')}.md.profile",
                f"{old_profile_path.replace('.profile', '')}.profile.md"
            ]
            for old_markdown_path in old_markdown_paths:
                if os.path.isfile(old_markdown_path):
                    os.remove(old_markdown_path)
                    logger.info(f"Deleted old format markdown: {old_markdown_path}")

    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Learned rules: short instructions stored in `enrich.md`
    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    @staticmethod
    def _parse_rules(content: str) -> List[Dict[str, str]]:
        """
        Split an enrichment file into its ``## <title>`` rule blocks.

        :param content: Enrichment markdown.
        :return: ``{"title", "content"}`` dicts, file order preserved.
        """
        content = content or ""
        headings = list(RULE_HEADING_PATTERN.finditer(content))

        rules: List[Dict[str, str]] = []
        for index, heading in enumerate(headings):
            start = heading.end()
            end = headings[index + 1].start() if index + 1 < len(headings) else len(content)
            rules.append({
                "title": heading.group("title").strip(),
                "content": content[start:end].strip("\n"),
            })
        return rules

    @staticmethod
    def _render_rules(rules: List[Dict[str, str]]) -> str:
        """
        Render parsed rules back into the enrichment markdown format.

        :param rules: ``{"title", "content"}`` dicts.
        :return: Enrichment file content (empty string when no rules).
        """
        blocks = [
            f"## {rule['title']}\n\n{rule['content'].strip()}".strip()
            for rule in rules
            if (rule.get("title") or "").strip()
        ]
        return ("\n\n".join(blocks).strip() + "\n") if blocks else ""

    def profile_rules(
        self,
        profile_name: str,
        include_inherited: bool = True
    ) -> List[Dict[str, Any]]:
        """
        List the learned rules of a profile for this project.

        Rules come from the ``enrich.md`` of every level between the level that
        owns the profile and this project (outermost first). Only the rules of
        THIS project are editable: parent and base rules are inherited and
        read-only.

        :param profile_name: Profile name.
        :param include_inherited: Include the rules learned by parent levels.
        :return: ``{"title", "content", "source", "path", "editable"}`` dicts.
        """
        if not profile_name:
            return []

        chain = self.profile_chain()
        owner_index = -1
        for index, manager in enumerate(chain):
            if manager.owns_profile(profile_name):
                owner_index = index

        rules: List[Dict[str, Any]] = []
        for manager in chain[owner_index + 1:]:
            editable = manager.settings.project_id == self.settings.project_id
            if not include_inherited and not editable:
                continue
            path = manager.profile_enrich_path(profile_name)
            for rule in self._parse_rules(self._read_text(path)):
                rules.append({
                    "title": rule["title"],
                    "content": rule["content"],
                    "source": manager.settings.project_name or "project",
                    "path": path,
                    "editable": editable,
                })
        return rules

    def find_profile_rule(
        self,
        profile_name: str,
        title: str,
        editable_only: bool = False
    ) -> Optional[Dict[str, Any]]:
        """
        Find a learned rule by title.

        :param profile_name: Profile name.
        :param title: Rule title (case/whitespace insensitive).
        :param editable_only: Only consider rules learned by this project.
        :return: The matching rule, or None.
        """
        wanted = normalize_rule_title(title)
        if not wanted:
            return None
        # Rules are listed outermost first: reversed() takes the most specific
        # (closest to this project) match first.
        for rule in reversed(self.profile_rules(profile_name)):
            if normalize_rule_title(rule["title"]) != wanted:
                continue
            if editable_only and not rule["editable"]:
                continue
            return rule
        return None

    def upsert_profile_rule(
        self,
        profile_name: str,
        title: str,
        text: str
    ) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        """
        Learn (create or replace) a RULE in this project's profile enrichment.

        A rule is a short instruction that is composed into the profile content
        and therefore reaches every chat. Writing an existing title replaces its
        block, so instructions are never duplicated.

        :param profile_name: Profile being enriched.
        :param title: Rule title (its identifier inside ``enrich.md``).
        :param text: Markdown instructions.
        :return: ``{"path", "title", "created", "rules"}``.

        :raises ValueError: On invalid input or when the rule budget is full.
        """
        profile_name = (profile_name or "").strip()
        title = " ".join((title or "").split()).strip()
        text = (text or "").strip()

        if not profile_name:
            raise ValueError("profile_name is required")
        if not title:
            raise ValueError(
                "title is required: it is the identifier used to update or "
                "forget the rule later"
            )
        if not text:
            raise ValueError("content is required: write the instruction to remember")
        if len(text) > MAX_RULE_CHARS:
            raise ValueError(
                f"The rule has {len(text)} characters; a rule holds at most "
                f"{MAX_RULE_CHARS} because it is injected into every chat. Store "
                "the long material as a knowledge file instead."
            )
        if not self.profile_exists(profile_name):
            raise ValueError(
                f"Unknown profile '{profile_name}': it does not exist in this "
                "project, in a parent project or in the base profiles."
            )

        enrich_path = self.profile_enrich_path(profile_name)
        os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(enrich_path), exist_ok=True)

        rules = self._parse_rules(self._read_text(enrich_path))
        wanted = normalize_rule_title(title)
        existing_titles = [normalize_rule_title(rule["title"]) for rule in rules]
        created = wanted not in existing_titles

        if created and len(rules) >= MAX_PROFILE_RULES:
            raise ValueError(
                f"Profile '{profile_name}' already has {len(rules)} rules (max "
                f"{MAX_PROFILE_RULES}). Promote or forget some of them, or store "
                "this content as a knowledge file."
            )

        rules = [
            rule for rule in rules
            if normalize_rule_title(rule["title"]) != wanted
        ]
        rules.append({"title": title, "content": text})

        with open(enrich_path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
            f.write(self._render_rules(rules))

        logger.info(
            "Profile '%s' %s rule '%s' in project '%s' (%s)",
            profile_name,
            "created" if created else "updated",
            title,
            self.settings.project_name,
            enrich_path,
        )
        return {
            "path": enrich_path,
            "title": title,
            "created": created,
            "rules": len(rules),
        }

    def delete_profile_rule(self, profile_name: str, title: str) -> str:
        """
        Forget a rule learned by THIS project.

        Inherited rules (parent projects and base profile) are read-only: they
        can only be removed from the level that learned them.

        :param profile_name: Profile name.
        :param title: Rule title.
        :return: Path of the enrichment file.

        :raises ValueError: If the rule is not found at this level.
        """
        profile_name = (profile_name or "").strip()
        if not profile_name:
            raise ValueError("profile_name is required")

        wanted = normalize_rule_title(title)
        if not wanted:
            raise ValueError("title is required: the rule identifier to forget")

        enrich_path = self.profile_enrich_path(profile_name)
        rules = self._parse_rules(self._read_text(enrich_path))
        kept = [
            rule for rule in rules
            if normalize_rule_title(rule["title"]) != wanted
        ]

        if len(kept) == len(rules):
            raise ValueError(
                f"Rule '{title}' was not learned by project "
                f"'{self.settings.project_name}'; inherited rules are read-only."
            )

        with open(enrich_path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
            f.write(self._render_rules(kept))

        logger.info(
            "Profile '%s' forgot rule '%s' in project '%s'",
            profile_name,
            title,
            self.settings.project_name,
        )
        return enrich_path

    def profile_knowledge_overview(self, profile_name: str) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        """
        Summarize everything a profile has learned for this project.

        Used by the ``overview`` action of the ``profile_knowledge`` tool so the
        model can decide what to read, forget or promote.

        :param profile_name: Profile name.
        :return: Rules, knowledge files, writable locations and limits.
        """
        rules = self.profile_rules(profile_name)
        files = self.list_profile_knowledge(profile_name)
        enrich_path = self.profile_enrich_path(profile_name)
        own_rules = [rule for rule in rules if rule["editable"]]

        return {
            "profile": profile_name,
            "rules": rules,
            "rules_count": len(rules),
            "own_rules_count": len(own_rules),
            "rules_chars": sum(len(rule["content"]) for rule in rules),
            "rules_file": enrich_path,
            "rules_file_exists": os.path.isfile(enrich_path),
            "knowledge_files": files,
            "knowledge_folder": self.profile_knowledge_path(profile_name),
            "limits": {
                "max_rule_chars": MAX_RULE_CHARS,
                "max_rules": MAX_PROFILE_RULES,
            },
        }

    def add_profile_instructions(
        self,
        profile_name: str,
        text: str,
        title: Optional[str] = None
    ) -> str:
        """
        Learn a rule (kept for backwards compatibility).

        Delegates to :meth:`upsert_profile_rule`: the text is stored as a
        ``## <title>`` block in ``<profiles>/<Name>/enrich.md`` and composed
        into the profile content from the next read on.

        :param profile_name: Profile being enriched.
        :param text: Markdown instructions to remember.
        :param title: Rule title (a dated title is used when omitted).
        :return: Path of the enrichment file.
        """
        result = self.upsert_profile_rule(
            profile_name=profile_name,
            title=title or f"Learned instructions ({datetime.now():%Y-%m-%d})",
            text=text,
        )
        return result["path"]

    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Knowledge files
    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    def profile_knowledge_roots(self, profile_name: str) -> List[Dict[str, str]]:
        """
        Resolve every knowledge folder visible for a profile, in chain order.

        Order: built-in base, then the project levels from the outermost parent
        down to this project. Missing folders are skipped.

        :param profile_name: Profile name.
        :return: List of ``{"source", "path"}`` dicts.
        """
        if not profile_name:
            return []

        roots: List[Dict[str, str]] = [{
            "source": "base",
            "path": self.base_profile_knowledge_path(profile_name),
        }]
        for manager in self.profile_chain():
            roots.append({
                "source": manager.settings.project_name or "project",
                "path": manager.profile_knowledge_path(profile_name),
            })
        return [root for root in roots if os.path.isdir(root["path"])]

    def list_profile_knowledge(self, profile_name: str) -> List[Dict[str, Any]]:
        """
        List the text knowledge files available for a profile.

        :param profile_name: Profile name.
        :return: List of ``{source, path, file, size}`` dicts.
        """
        files: List[Dict[str, Any]] = []
        for root in self.profile_knowledge_roots(profile_name):
            for file_path in sorted(pathlib.Path(root["path"]).rglob("*")):
                if not file_path.is_file():
                    continue
                if file_path.suffix.lower() not in TEXT_KNOWLEDGE_EXTENSIONS:
                    continue
                files.append({
                    "source": root["source"],
                    "path": str(file_path),
                    "file": os.path.relpath(str(file_path), root["path"]),
                    "size": file_path.stat().st_size,
                })
        return files

    def _resolve_knowledge_file(
        self,
        profile_name: str,
        file_name: str
    ) -> Optional[Dict[str, Any]]:
        """
        Find a knowledge file by its relative path within its knowledge folder.

        :param profile_name: Profile name.
        :param file_name: Path relative to the knowledge folder.
        :return: The matching entry, or None.
        """
        wanted = (file_name or "").strip().replace("\\", "/").lstrip("/")
        if not wanted:
            return None
        for entry in self.list_profile_knowledge(profile_name):
            if entry["file"].replace("\\", "/") == wanted:
                return entry
        return None

    def read_profile_knowledge(self, profile_name: str, file_name: str) -> str:
        """
        Read one knowledge file of a profile (base or any project level).

        :param profile_name: Profile name.
        :param file_name: Path relative to the knowledge folder.
        :return: File content.

        :raises ValueError: If the file is not found.
        """
        entry = self._resolve_knowledge_file(profile_name, file_name)
        if not entry:
            raise ValueError(
                f"Knowledge file '{file_name}' not found for profile "
                f"'{profile_name}'."
            )
        return self._read_text(entry["path"])

    def save_profile_knowledge(
        self,
        profile_name: str,
        file_name: str,
        content: str,
        overwrite: bool = False
    ) -> str:
        """
        Create or update a knowledge file for a profile in THIS project.

        Knowledge always lands in the current project, so a project can keep its
        own reference material without touching the base profile.

        :param profile_name: Profile name.
        :param file_name: Path relative to the knowledge folder.
        :param content: File content.
        :param overwrite: Replace the file when it already exists.
        :return: Path of the written file.

        :raises ValueError: On invalid input or unexpected overwrite.
        """
        profile_name = (profile_name or "").strip()
        if not profile_name:
            raise ValueError("profile_name is required")
        if not self.profile_exists(profile_name):
            raise ValueError(f"Unknown profile '{profile_name}'.")
        if content is None or not str(content).strip():
            raise ValueError("content is required")

        relative_path = self._validate_knowledge_file_name(file_name)
        knowledge_path = self.profile_knowledge_path(profile_name)
        target_path = os.path.join(knowledge_path, relative_path)

        if os.path.isfile(target_path) and not overwrite:
            raise ValueError(
                f"Knowledge file '{relative_path}' already exists for profile "
                f"'{profile_name}'. Read it first and use overwrite=True to "
                "replace it."
            )

        os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(target_path), exist_ok=True)
        with open(target_path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
            f.write(str(content))

        logger.info(
            "Profile '%s' knowledge saved by project '%s': %s",
            profile_name,
            self.settings.project_name,
            target_path,
        )
        return target_path

    def delete_profile_knowledge(self, profile_name: str, file_name: str) -> str:
        """
        Delete a knowledge file of THIS project's profile knowledge folder.

        Base and parent knowledge folders are read-only: only the current
        project's files can be deleted.

        :param profile_name: Profile name.
        :param file_name: Path relative to the knowledge folder.
        :return: Path of the deleted file.

        :raises ValueError: If the file is not owned by this project.
        """
        relative_path = self._validate_knowledge_file_name(file_name)
        knowledge_path = self.profile_knowledge_path(profile_name)
        target_path = os.path.join(knowledge_path, relative_path)

        if not os.path.isfile(target_path):
            raise ValueError(
                f"Knowledge file '{relative_path}' does not exist in this "
                f"project for profile '{profile_name}'. Base and parent "
                "knowledge files are read-only."
            )

        os.remove(target_path)
        logger.info(
            "Profile '%s' knowledge deleted: %s", profile_name, target_path
        )
        return target_path

    @staticmethod
    def _validate_knowledge_file_name(file_name: str) -> str:
        """
        Validate a knowledge file name (relative, text extension only).

        :param file_name: Candidate relative path.
        :return: Validated relative path (``.md`` added when missing).

        :raises ValueError: If the path escapes the knowledge folder or the
            extension is not a text one.
        """
        name = (file_name or "").strip().replace("\\", "/").lstrip("/")
        if not name:
            raise ValueError("file_name is required")
        if ".." in name.split("/"):
            raise ValueError(f"file_name cannot contain '..': {file_name!r}")
        if not os.path.splitext(name)[1]:
            name = f"{name}.md"
        extension = os.path.splitext(name)[1].lower()
        if extension not in TEXT_KNOWLEDGE_EXTENSIONS:
            raise ValueError(
                f"Unsupported knowledge file extension '{extension}'. Allowed: "
                f"{', '.join(sorted(TEXT_KNOWLEDGE_EXTENSIONS))}"
            )
        return name

    def search_profile_knowledge(
        self,
        profile_name: str,
        query: str,
        limit: int = 10
    ) -> List[Dict[str, Any]]:
        """
        Search the profile knowledge folders (base + every project level).

        The search is a plain case-insensitive term match on the filesystem: no
        indexing is required, so a file is searchable as soon as it is written.
        It is the fallback used when the semantic index is not available.

        :param profile_name: Profile name.
        :param query: Search terms (whitespace separated, OR matched).
        :param limit: Maximum number of files returned.
        :return: Matching entries with ``matches`` count and an ``excerpt``.
        """
        terms = [term for term in re.split(r"\s+", (query or "").strip().lower()) if term]
        if not terms:
            raise ValueError("query is required")

        limit = max(1, min(int(limit or 10), 50))
        results: List[Dict[str, Any]] = []

        for entry in self.list_profile_knowledge(profile_name):
            text = self._read_text(entry["path"])
            if not text:
                continue
            lines = text.splitlines()
            hits = [
                index for index, line in enumerate(lines)
                if any(term in line.lower() for term in terms)
            ]
            if not hits:
                continue
            start = max(hits[0] - EXCERPT_CONTEXT_LINES, 0)
            end = min(hits[0] + EXCERPT_CONTEXT_LINES + 1, len(lines))
            results.append({
                **entry,
                "matches": len(hits),
                "excerpt": "\n".join(lines[start:end]).strip(),
            })

        results.sort(key=lambda result: result["matches"], reverse=True)
        return results[:limit]

    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Promotion: decide between a rule (prompt) and a knowledge file (index)
    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    def promote_profile_rule_to_knowledge(
        self,
        profile_name: str,
        title: str,
        file_name: Optional[str] = None,
        delete_rule: bool = True
    ) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        """
        Move a learned rule into an indexed knowledge file.

        Used when a rule grew too long (or too specific) to stay in the prompt of
        every chat: the content becomes a knowledge file, retrieved on demand,
        and the rule is removed unless ``delete_rule`` is False.

        :param profile_name: Profile name.
        :param title: Title of a rule learned by this project.
        :param file_name: Target knowledge file (defaults to a slug of the title).
        :param delete_rule: Forget the rule after writing the file.
        :return: ``{"profile", "title", "file", "path", "rule_deleted"}``.

        :raises ValueError: When the rule does not exist at this level.
        """
        profile_name = (profile_name or "").strip()
        if not profile_name:
            raise ValueError("profile_name is required")

        rule = self.find_profile_rule(profile_name, title, editable_only=True)
        if not rule:
            raise ValueError(
                f"Rule '{title}' was not learned by project "
                f"'{self.settings.project_name}'. Inherited rules are read-only: "
                "promote them from the project that owns them."
            )

        relative_path = self._validate_knowledge_file_name(
            file_name or f"{slugify_rule_title(rule['title'])}.md"
        )
        content = f"# {rule['title']}\n\n{rule['content'].strip()}\n"
        path = self.save_profile_knowledge(
            profile_name=profile_name,
            file_name=relative_path,
            content=content,
            overwrite=True,
        )

        if delete_rule:
            self.delete_profile_rule(profile_name=profile_name, title=rule["title"])

        logger.info(
            "Profile '%s' promoted rule '%s' to knowledge file '%s'",
            profile_name,
            rule["title"],
            relative_path,
        )
        return {
            "profile": profile_name,
            "title": rule["title"],
            "file": relative_path,
            "path": path,
            "rule_deleted": bool(delete_rule),
        }

    def promote_profile_knowledge_to_rule(
        self,
        profile_name: str,
        file_name: str,
        title: Optional[str] = None,
        delete_file: bool = True
    ) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        """
        Turn a (short) knowledge file into a rule.

        Used when a document is really a durable instruction that must be present
        in every chat. The content must fit in a rule, otherwise it must be
        summarised first.

        :param profile_name: Profile name.
        :param file_name: Knowledge file path relative to the knowledge folder.
        :param title: Rule title (defaults to the file name).
        :param delete_file: Delete the file after learning the rule.
        :return: ``{"profile", "title", "path", "file_deleted"}``.

        :raises ValueError: When the file is missing or too long for a rule.
        """
        profile_name = (profile_name or "").strip()
        if not profile_name:
            raise ValueError("profile_name is required")

        content = self.read_profile_knowledge(
            profile_name=profile_name, file_name=file_name
        ).strip()

        if len(content) > MAX_RULE_CHARS:
            raise ValueError(
                f"'{file_name}' has {len(content)} characters; a rule holds at "
                f"most {MAX_RULE_CHARS} because it is injected into every chat. "
                "Summarise it into a short imperative rule and keep the file for "
                "the detail."
            )

        rule_title = (title or "").strip() or self._rule_title_from_file(file_name)
        result = self.upsert_profile_rule(
            profile_name=profile_name, title=rule_title, text=content
        )

        deleted = False
        if delete_file:
            try:
                self.delete_profile_knowledge(
                    profile_name=profile_name, file_name=file_name
                )
                deleted = True
            except ValueError as ex:
                logger.warning(
                    "Knowledge file '%s' not deleted after promotion: %s",
                    file_name,
                    ex,
                )

        return {
            "profile": profile_name,
            "title": rule_title,
            "path": result["path"],
            "file_deleted": deleted,
        }

    @staticmethod
    def _rule_title_from_file(file_name: str) -> str:
        """
        Derive a readable rule title from a knowledge file name.

        :param file_name: Knowledge file path relative to its folder.
        :return: Title-cased file stem (or a generic title).
        """
        stem = os.path.splitext(os.path.basename(file_name or ""))[0]
        title = re.sub(r"[-_]+", " ", stem).strip()
        return title or "Learned rule"

    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Profile matching & team helpers
    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    def is_profile_match(self, profile: Profile, file_path: str):
        try:
            return profile.file_match and re.search(profile.file_match, file_path)
        except:
            return False

    def get_file_profiles_by_file_path(self, file_path: str):
        file_profiles = [profile for profile in self.list_all_profiles() \
          if self.is_profile_match(profile=profile, file_path=file_path)]
        return self.reduce_linked_profiles(profiles=file_profiles)

    def get_profiles_by_name(self, profiles: []):
        return [p for p in self.list_all_profiles() if p.name in profiles]

    def get_profile_content_context(self, profile: Profile):
        return {
          "project_path": lambda: self.settings.abs_project_path,
          "project_name": lambda: self.settings.project_name,
          # "project_tree": lambda: generate_llm_tree(self.settings.abs_project_path)
        }

    def get_profile_With_content(self, profile: Profile):
        """
        Compose a profile for this project: own content + project enrichment.

        Every caller keeps using this method, so no other module needs to know
        that projects can enrich profiles.

        Profile tools are NOT modified here: the agent (SmolAgent) decides which
        profile tools are injected into each request, because it depends on the
        user (who may or may not be allowed to learn) and on the chat turn.

        :param profile: Profile to compose.
        :return: The same profile instance, with the composed content.
        """
        if profile:
            profile.content = self.compose_profile_content(profile)

        context = self.get_profile_content_context(profile=profile)
        
        # Regex explains:
        # {{    -> Matches literal opening braces
        # \s*   -> Matches optional whitespace
        # (\w+) -> Captures the variable name (alphanumeric/underscore)
        # \s*   -> Matches optional whitespace
        # }}    -> Matches literal closing braces
        pattern = r'\{\{\s*(\w+)\s*\}\}'

        def replacement_logic(match):
            variable_name = match.group(1)
            # Returns the value if found, otherwise keeps the original {{var}} text
            fnc = context.get(variable_name, None)
            if fnc:
                return str(fnc())
            return match.group(0)

        profile.parsed_content = re.sub(pattern, replacement_logic, profile.content or "")
        return profile

    def _profiles_by_name_registry(self) -> Dict[str, Profile]:
        """
        Build a ``name -> Profile`` index of every available profile.

        Building the index once avoids repeated (and expensive) full profile
        scans while resolving linked profile names recursively.

        :return: Mapping of profile name to profile entity (with parsed content).
        """
        return {
            profile.name: profile
            for profile in self.list_all_profiles()
            if profile and profile.name
        }

    def _expand_linked_profiles(
        self,
        profiles: List[Profile],
        seen_names: Optional[Set[str]] = None
    ) -> List[Profile]:
        """
        Expand a list of profiles with every profile they link to, recursively.

        Algorithm (one pass per profile, breadth-first):

        1. For each incoming profile we take its **name**.
        2. We find the profile entity for that name (from the registry of all
           available profiles).
        3. We read the entity's ``profiles`` property — a list of linked profile
           **names**.
        4. For every linked name we resolve the profile entity and queue it, so
           the operation repeats until no new profile is found.

        Deduplication is done by profile **name** (never by object equality),
        which makes the resolution deterministic and idempotent, and preserves
        the order in which profiles are discovered.

        :param profiles: Profiles referenced directly by the caller (the chat
                         mentions, file profiles, ...).
        :param seen_names: Optional set of already-resolved profile names,
                           shared across calls to safely ignore circular links.
        :return: The input profiles plus all their (recursively) linked profiles,
                 with no duplicates.
        """
        if seen_names is None:
            seen_names = set()

        # Resolve every linked name against this single snapshot of the
        # available profiles (avoids repeated, inconsistent disk reads).
        registry = self._profiles_by_name_registry()

        resolved: List[Profile] = []
        pending: List[Profile] = [p for p in (profiles or []) if p and p.name]

        while pending:
            profile = pending.pop(0)

            if profile.name in seen_names:
                continue
            seen_names.add(profile.name)

            # Prefer the entity loaded from the registry: it carries the
            # parsed content for use in the system prompt.
            entity = registry.get(profile.name) or profile
            resolved.append(entity)

            # Read the "profiles" property: the list of linked profile names.
            for linked_name in (entity.profiles or []):
                if not linked_name or linked_name in seen_names:
                    continue
                linked_profile = registry.get(linked_name)
                if linked_profile:
                    pending.append(linked_profile)
                else:
                    logger.warning(
                        "Profile '%s' links to unknown profile '%s'",
                        entity.name,
                        linked_name
                    )

        logger.info(
            "Expanded %d profile(s) into %d profile(s) following linked profiles: %s",
            len(profiles or []),
            len(resolved),
            [p.name for p in resolved]
        )
        return resolved

    def get_all_linked_profiles(self, profile: Profile, seen: set = None) -> List[Profile]:
        """
        Return *profile* plus every profile it links to, resolving links
        recursively by profile NAME (see :meth:`_expand_linked_profiles`).

        :param profile: The profile whose links to expand.
        :param seen: Optional set of already-resolved profile names.
        :return: The profile plus all (recursively) linked profiles.
        """
        if not profile or not profile.name:
            return []
        seen_names: Set[str] = set(seen or {})
        return self._expand_linked_profiles(profiles=[profile], seen_names=seen_names)

    def reduce_linked_profiles(self, profiles: List[Profile]) -> List[Profile]:
        """
        Expand a list of profiles with all the profiles they link to,
        recursively, and return them without duplicates.

        For each profile name we find the profile entity, read its ``profiles``
        property (a list of profile names) and, for every linked name, repeat
        the operation until all profiles are loaded.

        :param profiles: Profiles referenced directly by the caller.
        :return: The input profiles plus all their (recursively) linked profiles.
        """
        return self._expand_linked_profiles(profiles=profiles, seen_names=set())

    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Team (ADDED): profiles the LLM can use in NEW tasks
    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    @staticmethod
    def profile_short_description(profile: Profile, max_length: int = 160) -> str:
        """
        Return a short one-line description of *profile* for the team table.

        Resolution order: ``Profile.description`` → first meaningful line of the
        profile content (markdown heading markers removed) → ``Profile.category``.
        Whitespace is collapsed (the description must stay inside a table cell)
        and the result is truncated to *max_length* characters.

        :param profile: The profile to describe.
        :param max_length: Maximum length of the returned description.
        :return: Single-line description (may be an empty string).
        """
        description = (profile.description or "").strip()

        if not description and profile.content:
            for line in profile.content.splitlines():
                candidate = line.strip().lstrip("#").strip()
                if candidate:
                    description = candidate
                    break

        if not description:
            description = profile.category or ""

        # Collapse newlines and repeated spaces so the table stays a table.
        description = " ".join(description.split())

        if len(description) > max_length:
            description = description[:max_length - 3].rstrip() + "..."

        return description

    def get_team_profiles(
        self,
        profiles: List[Profile],
        exclude: Optional[List[Profile]] = None
    ) -> List[Profile]:
        """
        Resolve the TEAM of the given profiles: the profiles the LLM can use in
        NEW tasks.

        A profile declares its team through the ``team`` property — a list of
        profile **names**, like ``profiles`` lists linked profiles. Unlike
        linked profiles:

        * team members are NOT composed into the system prompt; they are only
          offered as a table (name + short description),
        * their links are NOT expanded: a team member's own team is offered only
          once that profile becomes active in a chat.

        Profiles already active in the turn (*exclude*, i.e. the profiles being
        composed) are not offered again, and unknown names are logged and
        skipped. Resolution is best effort: a broken team reference never
        blocks the chat.

        :param profiles: Profiles active in the current turn.
        :param exclude: Profiles (or profile names) that must not be offered.
        :return: Resolved team profiles, deduplicated by name, order preserved.
        """
        if not profiles:
            return []

        registry = self._profiles_by_name_registry()

        excluded_names: Set[str] = set()
        for excluded in (exclude or []):
            if isinstance(excluded, Profile):
                excluded_names.add(excluded.name)
            elif isinstance(excluded, dict):
                excluded_names.add(str(excluded.get("name") or ""))
            else:
                excluded_names.add(str(excluded).lstrip("@"))

        team_profiles: List[Profile] = []
        seen_names: Set[str] = set()

        for profile in profiles:
            for team_name in (profile.team or []):
                # Mentions may declare the member as "@name".
                team_name = (team_name or "").strip().lstrip("@")
                if not team_name or team_name in seen_names \
                        or team_name in excluded_names:
                    continue

                team_profile = registry.get(team_name)
                if not team_profile:
                    logger.warning(
                        "Profile '%s' lists unknown team profile '%s'",
                        profile.name,
                        team_name
                    )
                    continue

                seen_names.add(team_name)
                team_profiles.append(team_profile)

        logger.info(
            "Resolved team of %s: %s",
            [p.name for p in profiles],
            [p.name for p in team_profiles]
        )
        return team_profiles

"""
Profile knowledge tool for codx-junior.

A profile learns **per project**, and what it learns is kept in two places:

* **Rules** — short, always-relevant instructions stored as ``## <title>``
  blocks in ``<profiles>/<Name>/enrich.md``. They are composed into the profile
  content, so they reach every chat prompt. Addressed by title: writing the same
  title again replaces the instruction (never duplicated), ``forget`` removes it.
* **Knowledge files** — reference material under
  ``<profiles>/<Name>/knowledge/**`` (guidelines, conventions, examples, docs).
  Indexed in a ``KnowledgeDB`` per knowledge folder
  (:mod:`codx.junior.profiles.profile_knowledge`) and retrieved on demand.

Both are resolved through the project inheritance chain
(:class:`~codx.junior.profiles.profile_manager.ProfileManager`): the base
profile first, then every parent project down to the current one. Only the
current project's resources are writable.

The tool is meant to be used **proactively**: a profile is expected to store
what it learns as the work happens, without waiting to be asked, and to choose
the cheaper store (rule vs file) depending on the size and lifetime of the
content.

Permissions:

* reading (``overview``, ``search``, ``read``) is available to any user working
  on the project;
* writing (``remember``, ``forget``, ``write_file``, ``delete_file``,
  ``promote``) requires a **codx-junior admin**, a **project admin** or a
  **project knowledge admin** (``knowledge_admin``), see
  :meth:`UserSecurityManager.can_manage_profile_knowledge`.

The tool is NOT part of the profile definition: the agent
(:class:`codx.junior.ai.smol.smol_agent.SmolAgent`) decides whether to inject it
into the request. The check is repeated here, so a tool call can never bypass
it.

Made with ❤️ by codx-junior
"""

import json
import logging
import os
from typing import Any, Dict, List, Optional

from codx.junior.model.model import CodxUser
from codx.junior.profiles.profile_knowledge import ProfileKnowledge
from codx.junior.profiles.profile_manager import (
    MAX_RULE_CHARS,
    ProfileManager,
)
from codx.junior.security.user_management import UserSecurityManager
from codx.junior.settings import CODXJuniorSettings
from .model import ToolResponse

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Actions
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

ACTION_OVERVIEW = "overview"
ACTION_SEARCH = "search"
ACTION_READ = "read"
ACTION_REMEMBER = "remember"
ACTION_FORGET = "forget"
ACTION_WRITE_FILE = "write_file"
ACTION_DELETE_FILE = "delete_file"
ACTION_PROMOTE = "promote"

# Read-only actions: available to every project user.
READ_ACTIONS = [ACTION_OVERVIEW, ACTION_SEARCH, ACTION_READ]

# Actions that modify what the profile knows: knowledge administration required.
WRITE_ACTIONS = [
    ACTION_REMEMBER,
    ACTION_FORGET,
    ACTION_WRITE_FILE,
    ACTION_DELETE_FILE,
    ACTION_PROMOTE,
]

VALID_ACTIONS = READ_ACTIONS + WRITE_ACTIONS

# Deprecated action names kept so older calls (and prompts) keep working.
ACTION_ALIASES = {
    "list": ACTION_OVERVIEW,
    "write_knowledge": ACTION_WRITE_FILE,
    "delete_knowledge": ACTION_DELETE_FILE,
}

# Promotion directions: decide between "always in the prompt" (rule) and
# "indexed, retrieved on demand" (knowledge file).
DIRECTION_RULE_TO_FILE = "rule_to_file"
DIRECTION_FILE_TO_RULE = "file_to_rule"
DIRECTIONS = [DIRECTION_RULE_TO_FILE, DIRECTION_FILE_TO_RULE]

# Number of matches returned to the model by default.
DEFAULT_LIMIT = 8

# A result chunk is injected into the model context: keep it bounded.
MAX_RESULT_CHARS = 1500

# Arguments are validated here too (cost/abuse guard, independent of the tool).
MAX_QUERY_CHARS = 500
MAX_FILE_NAME_CHARS = 500
MAX_FILE_ARG_CHARS = 200000

# Profiles inspected when no profile name is given (token/cost guard).
MAX_PROFILES_SCANNED = 10

# Characters of a rule shown by the `overview` action.
OVERVIEW_RULE_PREVIEW_CHARS = 160

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Permission helpers
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def _current_user(
    settings: Optional[CODXJuniorSettings] = None,
    session: Any = None
) -> Optional[CodxUser]:
    """
    Resolve the user executing the tool.

    Tools get ``session`` injected (``ToolSettings.session``) or, when they only
    receive ``settings``, the active session attached to them.

    Args:
        settings: Project settings.
        session: Active session, when injected.

    Returns:
        The ``CodxUser`` behind the call, or None when unknown.
    """
    user = getattr(session, "user", None)
    if user:
        return user
    active_session = getattr(settings, "_active_session", None)
    return getattr(active_session, "user", None)


def _require_knowledge_permission(
    settings: Optional[CODXJuniorSettings],
    user: Optional[CodxUser]
) -> None:
    """
    Ensure the user can modify what the profiles learn in the project.

    The rule lives in :meth:`UserSecurityManager.can_manage_profile_knowledge`
    so the agent (which decides whether to offer this tool) and the tool itself
    always agree: codx-junior admins, project admins and project knowledge
    admins (``knowledge_admin``) are allowed.

    Args:
        settings: Project settings.
        user: User executing the tool.

    Raises:
        PermissionError: When the user has no knowledge administration rights.
    """
    if not user or not getattr(user, "username", ""):
        raise PermissionError(
            "Learning requires an authenticated user with profile knowledge "
            "administration rights."
        )

    try:
        allowed = UserSecurityManager().can_manage_profile_knowledge(
            user=user, settings=settings
        )
    except Exception as ex:
        logger.warning(
            "Could not resolve profile knowledge permission for '%s': %s",
            user.username,
            ex,
        )
        allowed = False

    if allowed:
        return

    raise PermissionError(
        f"User '{user.username}' cannot change what profiles learn in project "
        f"'{(settings.project_name if settings else '')}'. Only a project admin, "
        "a project knowledge admin or a codx-junior admin can do it."
    )


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Formatting helpers
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def _relative_to_project(settings: CODXJuniorSettings, path: str) -> str:
    """
    Render a path relative to the project root when possible.

    Args:
        settings: Project settings.
        path: Absolute or relative path.

    Returns:
        The path relative to the project root, or the original path.
    """
    project_path = getattr(settings, "abs_project_path", None)
    if project_path and path and path.startswith(project_path):
        return os.path.relpath(path, project_path)
    return path


def _validate_text(value: Optional[str], label: str, max_chars: int) -> str:
    """
    Validate a free-text argument.

    Args:
        value: Raw argument value.
        label: Argument name used in the error message.
        max_chars: Maximum accepted length.

    Returns:
        The stripped value.

    Raises:
        ValueError: When the value is empty or too long.
    """
    text = (value or "").strip()
    if not text:
        raise ValueError(f"{label} is required")
    if len(text) > max_chars:
        raise ValueError(
            f"{label} has {len(text)} characters; the maximum is {max_chars}."
        )
    return text


def _excerpt(content: str) -> str:
    """
    Truncate a document chunk to the maximum excerpt size.

    Args:
        content: Chunk content.

    Returns:
        Excerpt (with an ellipsis when truncated).
    """
    content = (content or "").strip()
    if len(content) <= MAX_RESULT_CHARS:
        return content
    return content[:MAX_RESULT_CHARS].rstrip() + "\n..."


def _score(result: Dict[str, Any]) -> float:
    """
    Safely read the relevance score of a search result.

    Args:
        result: Result dict.

    Returns:
        Score as float, 0 when it cannot be converted.
    """
    try:
        return float(result.get("score") or 0.0)
    except (TypeError, ValueError):
        return 0.0


def _knowledge_table(
    entries: List[Dict[str, Any]],
    settings: CODXJuniorSettings
) -> str:
    """
    Render the knowledge file list as a Markdown table.

    Args:
        entries: Entries returned by ``ProfileManager.list_profile_knowledge``.
        settings: Project settings (for relative paths).

    Returns:
        Markdown table (or a "no knowledge" note).
    """
    if not entries:
        return "> No knowledge files yet."

    lines = [
        f"> {len(entries)} knowledge file(s)",
        "",
        "**File** | **Source** | **Size** | **Path**",
        "---|---|---|---",
    ]
    for entry in entries:
        lines.append(
            f"`{entry['file']}` | {entry['source']} | {entry['size']} B | "
            f"`{_relative_to_project(settings, entry['path'])}`"
        )
    return "\n".join(lines)


def _first_line(text: str, max_chars: int = OVERVIEW_RULE_PREVIEW_CHARS) -> str:
    """
    Return the first meaningful line of a text block.

    Args:
        text: Block content.
        max_chars: Maximum length of the returned line.

    Returns:
        Single-line preview.
    """
    for line in (text or "").splitlines():
        candidate = " ".join(line.split())
        if candidate:
            return candidate[:max_chars]
    return ""


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Search (semantic index with filesystem fallback)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def _semantic_search(
    settings: CODXJuniorSettings,
    profiles: List[str],
    query: str,
    limit: int
) -> List[Dict[str, Any]]:
    """
    Search the profile knowledge using the semantic index.

    Each knowledge folder has its own ``KnowledgeDB`` (see
    :class:`~codx.junior.profiles.profile_knowledge.ProfileKnowledge`), which is
    indexed lazily on every call.

    Args:
        settings: Project settings.
        profiles: Profiles to search.
        query: Natural-language query.
        limit: Maximum number of results.

    Returns:
        Normalized results: ``profile``, ``level``, ``file``, ``path``,
        ``score`` and ``excerpt``.
    """
    knowledge = ProfileKnowledge(settings=settings)
    results = knowledge.search(query=query, profile_names=profiles, limit=limit)
    return [
        {
            "profile": result.get("profile", ""),
            "level": result.get("knowledge_source", ""),
            "file": result.get("file", ""),
            "path": result.get("source", ""),
            "score": _score(result),
            "excerpt": result.get("content", ""),
        }
        for result in results
    ]


def _term_search(
    manager: ProfileManager,
    profiles: List[str],
    query: str,
    limit: int
) -> List[Dict[str, Any]]:
    """
    Search the profile knowledge with a plain case-insensitive term match.

    Fallback used when the semantic index is unavailable (no embeddings model,
    index error, ...), so the profile can still find what it wrote.

    Args:
        manager: Project ProfileManager.
        profiles: Profiles to search.
        query: Search terms.
        limit: Maximum number of results.

    Returns:
        Normalized results (see :func:`_semantic_search`), unranked (0.0).
    """
    results: List[Dict[str, Any]] = []
    for profile_name in profiles:
        for entry in manager.search_profile_knowledge(
            profile_name=profile_name, query=query, limit=limit
        ):
            results.append({
                "profile": profile_name,
                "level": entry.get("source", ""),
                "file": entry.get("file", ""),
                "path": entry.get("path", ""),
                "score": 0.0,
                "excerpt": entry.get("excerpt", ""),
            })
    return results[:limit]


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Actions
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def _action_overview(
    manager: ProfileManager,
    settings: CODXJuniorSettings,
    profile_name: str,
    profiles: List[str]
) -> ToolResponse:
    """
    Summarize what a profile has learned for this project.

    Args:
        manager: Project ProfileManager.
        settings: Project settings.
        profile_name: Profile to inspect (empty to list profiles with material).
        profiles: Profiles that have knowledge or rules (fallback listing).

    Returns:
        ToolResponse with the overview (user) and the structured state (model).
    """
    if not profile_name:
        names = profiles or []
        if not names:
            return ToolResponse(
                user_response="> No profile has learned anything in this project yet.",
                llm_response=json.dumps(
                    {
                        "profiles": [],
                        "next": (
                            "Nothing stored yet. Use action='remember' for a short "
                            "durable rule or action='write_file' for reference "
                            "material."
                        ),
                    },
                    indent=2,
                ),
            )
        return ToolResponse(
            user_response="\n".join([
                f"### Profiles with learned material ({len(names)})",
                "",
                *[f"- `{name}`" for name in names],
            ]),
            llm_response=json.dumps(
                {
                    "profiles": names,
                    "next": (
                        "Call action='overview' with one of these 'profile_name' "
                        "values to inspect it."
                    ),
                },
                indent=2,
            ),
        )

    overview = manager.profile_knowledge_overview(profile_name)
    rules = overview["rules"]
    limits = overview["limits"]

    lines = [f"### Profile knowledge: `{profile_name}`", ""]
    if rules:
        lines.append(
            f"**Learned rules** — {overview['rules_count']} rule(s), "
            f"{overview['rules_chars']} chars (limit {limits['max_rule_chars']} "
            "chars/rule; these are injected in EVERY chat)"
        )
        for rule in rules:
            scope = "editable" if rule["editable"] else f"inherited: {rule['source']}"
            lines.append(
                f"- **{rule['title']}** ({len(rule['content'])} chars, {scope}) — "
                f"{_first_line(rule['content'])}"
            )
    else:
        lines.append("> No learned rules yet.")
    lines.append("")
    lines.append(_knowledge_table(overview["knowledge_files"], settings))
    lines.append("")
    lines.append(
        f"Rules file: `{_relative_to_project(settings, overview['rules_file'])}`"
    )
    lines.append(
        f"Knowledge folder: "
        f"`{_relative_to_project(settings, overview['knowledge_folder'])}/`"
    )
    lines.append(
        "\n> Use `read` (with `title` or `file_name`) to see the full content, "
        "`remember`/`forget` for rules, `write_file`/`delete_file` for files and "
        "`promote` to move content between the two."
    )

    llm_response = json.dumps(
        {
            "profile": profile_name,
            "rules": [
                {
                    "title": rule["title"],
                    "chars": len(rule["content"]),
                    "source": rule["source"],
                    "editable": rule["editable"],
                    "preview": _first_line(rule["content"]),
                }
                for rule in rules
            ],
            "knowledge_files": [
                {
                    "file": entry["file"],
                    "source": entry["source"],
                    "size": entry["size"],
                    "path": entry["path"],
                }
                for entry in overview["knowledge_files"]
            ],
            "rules_file": overview["rules_file"],
            "knowledge_folder": overview["knowledge_folder"],
            "limits": limits,
        },
        indent=2,
    )
    return ToolResponse(user_response="\n".join(lines), llm_response=llm_response)


def _action_search(
    manager: ProfileManager,
    settings: CODXJuniorSettings,
    profiles: List[str],
    query: str,
    limit: int
) -> ToolResponse:
    """
    Search what the profiles have learned (rules preview + knowledge matches).

    Args:
        manager: Project ProfileManager.
        settings: Project settings.
        profiles: Profiles to search.
        query: Search terms or natural-language question.
        limit: Maximum number of knowledge matches.

    Returns:
        ToolResponse with the excerpts (user) and the matches (model).
    """
    try:
        results = _semantic_search(
            settings=settings, profiles=profiles, query=query, limit=limit
        )
    except Exception as ex:
        logger.warning(
            "profile_knowledge: semantic search unavailable (%s); falling back to "
            "term search",
            ex,
        )
        results = _term_search(
            manager=manager, profiles=profiles, query=query, limit=limit
        )

    profiles_label = ", ".join(profiles)

    if not results:
        return ToolResponse(
            user_response=(
                f"✓ No profile knowledge matching `{query}` in {profiles_label}"
            ),
            llm_response=json.dumps(
                {
                    "profiles": profiles,
                    "query": query,
                    "count": 0,
                    "results": [],
                    "next": (
                        "Nothing matched. Do not invent knowledge: if the "
                        "information is durable, learn it now with "
                        "action='remember' (short rule) or action='write_file' "
                        "(reference material)."
                    ),
                },
                indent=2,
            ),
        )

    user_lines = [f"### Profile knowledge: {profiles_label}", f"> Query: `{query}`", ""]
    for result in results:
        user_lines.extend([
            f"**`{result['file'] or result['path']}`** — profile "
            f"`{result['profile']}` — {result['level']} — "
            f"score {_score(result):.4f}",
            f"`{_relative_to_project(settings, result['path'])}`",
            "",
            "```markdown",
            _excerpt(result["excerpt"]),
            "```",
            "",
        ])

    llm_response = json.dumps(
        {
            "profiles": profiles,
            "query": query,
            "count": len(results),
            "results": [
                {
                    "profile": result["profile"],
                    "level": result["level"],
                    "file": result["file"],
                    "path": result["path"],
                    "score": _score(result),
                    "content": _excerpt(result["excerpt"]),
                }
                for result in results
            ],
        },
        indent=2,
    )

    logger.info(
        "profile_knowledge: search '%s' in %s returned %d result(s)",
        query,
        profiles_label,
        len(results),
    )
    return ToolResponse(user_response="\n".join(lines := user_lines), llm_response=llm_response)


def _action_read(
    manager: ProfileManager,
    settings: CODXJuniorSettings,
    profile_name: str,
    title: Optional[str],
    file_name: Optional[str]
) -> ToolResponse:
    """
    Read a learned rule (by ``title``) or a knowledge file (by ``file_name``).

    Args:
        manager: Project ProfileManager.
        settings: Project settings.
        profile_name: Profile name.
        title: Rule title.
        file_name: Knowledge file path relative to the knowledge folder.

    Returns:
        ToolResponse with the content.

    Raises:
        ValueError: When neither argument is given or the resource is missing.
    """
    if title:
        rule = manager.find_profile_rule(profile_name=profile_name, title=title)
        if not rule:
            raise ValueError(
                f"Rule '{title}' not found for profile '{profile_name}'."
            )
        scope = "editable" if rule["editable"] else "inherited (read-only)"
        user_response = "\n".join([
            f"### Rule `{rule['title']}` — profile `{profile_name}`",
            f"> Level: **{rule['source']}** — {scope} — "
            f"`{_relative_to_project(settings, rule['path'])}`",
            "",
            "```markdown",
            rule["content"],
            "```",
        ])
        return ToolResponse(
            user_response=user_response,
            llm_response=json.dumps(
                {
                    "profile": profile_name,
                    "rule": rule["title"],
                    "source": rule["source"],
                    "path": rule["path"],
                    "editable": rule["editable"],
                    "content": rule["content"],
                },
                indent=2,
            ),
        )

    if not file_name:
        raise ValueError(
            "read requires 'title' (learned rule) or 'file_name' (knowledge file)"
        )

    content = manager.read_profile_knowledge(
        profile_name=profile_name, file_name=file_name
    )
    entry = manager._resolve_knowledge_file(profile_name, file_name) or {}

    user_response = "\n".join([
        f"### `{file_name}` — profile `{profile_name}`",
        f"> Level: **{entry.get('source', 'unknown')}** — "
        f"`{_relative_to_project(settings, entry.get('path', file_name))}`",
        "",
        "```markdown",
        content,
        "```",
    ])
    return ToolResponse(
        user_response=user_response,
        llm_response=json.dumps(
            {
                "profile": profile_name,
                "file": file_name,
                "source": entry.get("source", ""),
                "path": entry.get("path", ""),
                "content": content,
            },
            indent=2,
        ),
    )


def _action_remember(
    manager: ProfileManager,
    settings: CODXJuniorSettings,
    profile_name: str,
    title: Optional[str],
    content: Optional[str]
) -> ToolResponse:
    """
    Learn a RULE: create or replace a short instruction for this project.

    Args:
        manager: Project ProfileManager.
        settings: Project settings.
        profile_name: Profile to teach.
        title: Rule title (identifier).
        content: Instruction markdown.

    Returns:
        ToolResponse describing where the rule was stored.
    """
    text = _validate_text(content, "content", MAX_RULE_CHARS)
    rule_title = (title or "").strip() or _first_line(text, 60)
    result = manager.upsert_profile_rule(
        profile_name=profile_name, title=rule_title, text=text
    )

    user_response = "\n".join([
        f"### Rule {'created' if result['created'] else 'updated'} for "
        f"`{profile_name}`",
        "",
        f"- Title: **{result['title']}**",
        f"- Stored in: `{_relative_to_project(settings, result['path'])}`",
        f"- Rules now: {result['rules']} (each one is injected in every chat)",
        f"- Applies to: project **{settings.project_name}** and its children "
        "while they do not define the profile themselves",
        "",
        "```markdown",
        text,
        "```",
    ])
    return ToolResponse(
        user_response=user_response,
        llm_response=json.dumps(
            {
                "action": ACTION_REMEMBER,
                "profile": profile_name,
                "title": result["title"],
                "created": result["created"],
                "rules": result["rules"],
                "path": _relative_to_project(settings, result["path"]),
                "scope": settings.project_name,
            },
            indent=2,
        ),
    )


def _action_forget(
    manager: ProfileManager,
    settings: CODXJuniorSettings,
    profile_name: str,
    title: Optional[str]
) -> ToolResponse:
    """
    Forget a RULE learned by this project.

    Args:
        manager: Project ProfileManager.
        settings: Project settings.
        profile_name: Profile name.
        title: Rule title.

    Returns:
        ToolResponse confirming the removal.
    """
    rule_title = _validate_text(title, "title", MAX_QUERY_CHARS)
    path = manager.delete_profile_rule(profile_name=profile_name, title=rule_title)

    user_response = "\n".join([
        f"### Rule forgotten by `{profile_name}`",
        "",
        f"- Title: **{rule_title}**",
        f"- File: `{_relative_to_project(settings, path)}`",
        "",
        "> Inherited rules (parent projects, base profile) are read-only.",
    ])
    return ToolResponse(
        user_response=user_response,
        llm_response=json.dumps(
            {
                "action": ACTION_FORGET,
                "profile": profile_name,
                "title": rule_title,
                "path": _relative_to_project(settings, path),
            },
            indent=2,
        ),

def _action_write_file(

def _action_promote(
    manager: ProfileManager,
    settings: CODXJuniorSettings,
    profile_name: str,
    title: Optional[str],
    file_name: Optional[str],
    direction: Optional[str],
    keep_source: bool
) -> ToolResponse:
    """
    Move content between the two stores (rule ⇄ knowledge file).

    Args:
        manager: Project ProfileManager.
        settings: Project settings.
        profile_name: Profile name.
        title: Rule title (source or target depending on the direction).
        file_name: Knowledge file (source or target depending on the direction).
        direction: ``rule_to_file`` or ``file_to_rule``.
        keep_source: Keep the source after copying.

    Returns:
        ToolResponse describing the promotion.

    Raises:
        ValueError: On a missing/unknown direction or arguments.
    """
    direction = (direction or "").strip().lower()
    if direction not in DIRECTIONS:
        raise ValueError(
            f"promote requires 'direction': {', '.join(DIRECTIONS)}"
        )

    if direction == DIRECTION_RULE_TO_FILE:
        if not title:
            raise ValueError("promote rule_to_file requires 'title'")
        result = manager.promote_profile_rule_to_knowledge(
            profile_name=profile_name,
            title=title,
            file_name=file_name,
            delete_rule=not keep_source,
        )
        user_response = "\n".join([
            f"### Rule promoted to knowledge: `{profile_name}`",
            "",
            f"- Rule: **{result['title']}**",
            f"- File: `{_relative_to_project(settings, result['path'])}`",
            f"- Rule removed: {result['rule_deleted']}",
            "",
            "> It is now indexed and retrieved only when relevant, so it no "
            "longer costs prompt tokens on every chat.",
        ])
    else:
        if not file_name:
            raise ValueError("promote file_to_rule requires 'file_name'")
        result = manager.promote_profile_knowledge_to_rule(
            profile_name=profile_name,
            file_name=file_name,
            title=title,
            delete_file=not keep_source,
        )
        user_response = "\n".join([
            f"### Knowledge promoted to rule: `{profile_name}`",
            "",
            f"- Rule: **{result['title']}**",
            f"- Stored in: `{_relative_to_project(settings, result['path'])}`",
            f"- File removed: {result['file_deleted']}",
            "",
            "> It is now injected in every chat where the profile is active: "
            "keep rules short and imperative.",
        ])

    return ToolResponse(
        user_response=user_response,
        llm_response=json.dumps({"action": ACTION_PROMOTE, **result}, indent=2),
    )

def profile_knowledge(
    action: str,
    profile_name: Optional[str] = None,
    query: Optional[str] = None,
    file_name: Optional[str] = None,
    content: Optional[str] = None,
    title: Optional[str] = None,
    direction: Optional[str] = None,
    overwrite: bool = False,
    keep_source: bool = False,
    limit: int = DEFAULT_LIMIT,
    **kwargs
) -> ToolResponse:
    """
    Read, search and update what a profile has learned for this project.

    Actions:
        - ``overview``: rules + knowledge files + writable locations and limits.
        - ``search``: semantic search over the knowledge of one (or all) profile.
        - ``read``: read a rule (``title``) or a knowledge file (``file_name``).
        - ``remember``: create/replace a short RULE (``title`` + ``content``).
        - ``forget``: remove a rule (``title``).
        - ``write_file``: create/update a knowledge file (``file_name`` + ``content``).
        - ``delete_file``: remove a knowledge file (``file_name``).
        - ``promote``: move a rule to a file or a file to a rule (``direction``).

    Args:
        action: One of :data:`VALID_ACTIONS`.
        profile_name: Profile that learns or is consulted. Optional for
            ``overview`` (listing) and ``search`` (all profiles with knowledge).
        query: Search terms for ``search``.
        file_name: Knowledge file path relative to the profile knowledge folder.
        content: Rule text (``remember``) or file body (``write_file``).
        title: Rule title, used as its identifier.
        direction: ``rule_to_file`` or ``file_to_rule`` (``promote``).
        overwrite: Replace an existing knowledge file.
        keep_source: Keep the source when promoting.
        limit: Maximum number of search results (1-50).
        **kwargs: Internal. Injected by the agent runtime: ``settings``,
            ``session``.

    Returns:
        ToolResponse: ``user_response`` for the chat, ``llm_response`` with the
        machine-readable result for the model.

    Raises:
        Exception: If the project settings are missing.

    Example:
        >>> profile_knowledge("search", profile_name="software_developer",
        ...                   query="angular signals")
        >>> profile_knowledge("remember", profile_name="software_developer",
        ...                   title="Angular conventions",
        ...                   content="Always use standalone components.")
        >>> profile_knowledge("write_file", profile_name="software_developer",
        ...                   file_name="guidelines/state.md",
        ...                   content="# State management\\n...")
        >>> profile_knowledge("promote", profile_name="software_developer",
        ...                   direction="rule_to_file", title="Angular conventions")
    """
    settings: CODXJuniorSettings = kwargs.get("settings")
    if not settings:
        raise Exception("Invalid project settings")
    session = kwargs.get("session")
    if session is None:
        session = getattr(settings, "_active_session", None)

    action = (action or "").strip().lower()
    action = ACTION_ALIASES.get(action, action)
    if action not in VALID_ACTIONS:
        return ToolResponse(
            user_response=(
                f"❌ Invalid action `{action}`. Valid actions: "
                f"{', '.join(VALID_ACTIONS)}"
            ),
            llm_response=(
                f"Invalid action '{action}'. Valid actions: "
                f"{', '.join(VALID_ACTIONS)}"
            ),
        )

    manager = ProfileManager(settings=settings)
    profile_name = (profile_name or "").strip()

    try:
        if action in WRITE_ACTIONS:
            _require_knowledge_permission(
                settings=settings, user=_current_user(settings=settings, session=session)
            )

        if profile_name and not manager.profile_exists(profile_name):
            raise ValueError(
                f"Unknown profile '{profile_name}': it does not exist in this "
                "project, in a parent project or in the base profiles."
            )

        if action == ACTION_OVERVIEW:
            return _action_overview(
                manager=manager,
                settings=settings,
                profile_name=profile_name,
                profiles=(
                    manager.list_profiles()
                    and [
                        profile.name for profile in manager.list_profiles()
                        if manager.profile_rules(profile.name, include_inherited=False)
                        or manager.list_profile_knowledge(profile.name)
                    ][:MAX_PROFILES_SCANNED]
                ) or [],
            )

        if action == ACTION_SEARCH:
            query = _validate_text(query, "query", MAX_QUERY_CHARS)
            profiles = [profile_name] if profile_name else [
                profile.name for profile in manager.list_profiles()
                if manager.list_profile_knowledge(profile.name)
            ][:MAX_PROFILES_SCANNED]
            if not profiles:
                return ToolResponse(
                    user_response="> No profile knowledge found in this project.",
                    llm_response=json.dumps(
                        {
                            "profiles": [],
                            "query": query,
                            "count": 0,
                            "next": (
                                "No profile has a knowledge folder in this project "
                                "or its parents. Use action='write_file' (requires "
                                "project admin, project knowledge admin or "
                                "codx-junior admin) to create the first one."
                            ),
                        },
                        indent=2,
                    ),
                )
            return _action_search(
                manager=manager,
                settings=settings,
                profiles=profiles,
                query=query,
                limit=limit,
            )

        if not profile_name:
            raise ValueError(
                f"profile_name is required for '{action}': it is the profile that "
                "learns or forgets."
            )

        if action == ACTION_READ:
            return _action_read(
                manager=manager,
                settings=settings,
                profile_name=profile_name,
                title=title,
                file_name=file_name,
            )

        if action == ACTION_REMEMBER:
            return _action_remember(
                manager=manager,
                settings=settings,
                profile_name=profile_name,
                title=title,
                content=content,
            )

        if action == ACTION_FORGET:
            return _action_forget(
                manager=manager,
                settings=settings,
                profile_name=profile_name,
                title=title,
            )

        if action == ACTION_WRITE_FILE:
            return _action_write_file(
                manager=manager,
                settings=settings,
                profile_name=profile_name,
                file_name=file_name,
                content=content,
                overwrite=overwrite,
            )

        if action == ACTION_DELETE_FILE:
            return _action_delete_file(
                manager=manager,
                settings=settings,
                profile_name=profile_name,
                file_name=file_name,
            )

        return _action_promote(
            manager=manager,
            settings=settings,
            profile_name=profile_name,
            title=title,
            file_name=file_name,
            direction=direction,
            keep_source=keep_source,
        )

    except PermissionError as ex:
        logger.warning("profile_knowledge(%s): %s", action, ex)
        return ToolResponse(
            user_response=f"🔒 {ex}",
            llm_response=(
                f"profile_knowledge action '{action}' denied: {ex} Do not retry: "
                "keep working and mention it to the user, or ask for knowledge "
                "administration rights on the project."
            ),
        )
    except ValueError as ex:
        logger.warning("profile_knowledge(%s): %s", action, ex)
        return ToolResponse(
            user_response=f"❌ {ex}",
            llm_response=f"profile_knowledge action '{action}' failed: {ex}",
        )
    except Exception as ex:
        logger.exception("profile_knowledge(%s): unexpected error", action)
        return ToolResponse(
            user_response=f"❌ Error: {ex}",
            llm_response=f"profile_knowledge action '{action}' failed: {ex}",
        )


def profile_knowledge_search(
    query: str,
    profile_name: Optional[str] = None,
    limit: int = DEFAULT_LIMIT,
    **kwargs
) -> ToolResponse:
    """
    Read-only alias of :func:`profile_knowledge` (search only).

    Kept so the read-only tool registered for every profile user cannot write:
    any non-read action is rejected before touching the project.

    Args:
        query: Topic or question to look for in the profile knowledge.

    Returns:
        ToolResponse: matches (user) and machine-readable results (model).

    Example:
        >>> profile_knowledge_search("angular signals",
        ...                          profile_name="software_developer")
    """
    return profile_knowledge(
        action=ACTION_SEARCH,
        profile_name=profile_name,
        query=query,
        limit=limit,
        **kwargs
    )
